Author Sir Salman Rushdie has said he longs for the day when Donald Trump’s new White House ballroom and his proposed “Arc de Trump” are torn down.

Sir Salman denounced the “horrifying” behaviour of the “thin-skinned” US president and claimed the “cult” he had created was beginning to crumble.

In an exclusive interview with The Independent editor-in-chief Geordie Greig, he said he believed that once Trump was removed from power his beloved ballroom and triumphal arch would be removed too.

The “demolition of Trump” would be a day to celebrate, he said.

Sir Salman, who has lived in America since 2000 and holds British and American citizenship, said: “I look forward to the day when there is no more Trump and every ugly thing he's built gets torn down.”

He continued: “When the ballroom gets destroyed… this ridiculous triumphal arch… when that comes down, I think there'll be a moment of the demolition of Trump, which will be very pleasing to see.”

open image in gallery Salman Rushdie speaks to Geordie Greig on The Talk Show ( The Independent )

The proposed 250 feet triumphal arch in Washington – termed the ‘Arc de Trump’ by some – includes a golden-winged Lady Liberty on top, flanked by two golden eagles.

Trump had the east wing of the White House bulldozed last year to make way for a 400 million dollar ballroom currently under construction.

An attempt by America’s National Trust for Historic Preservation to stop the project was rejected by the Supreme Court last month in a 5-4 ruling in favour of Trump. The organisation argued the ballroom was an ‘aesthetic, cultural and historical’ affront.

Sir Salman called Trump a “brilliant liar” and claimed the President would break his promise to give $5,000 to all US adults if his Republican Party wins the coming mid term elections: “He stiffs people all the time.”

Sir Salman faced death threats for years over his 1988 book The Satanic Verses and only narrowly survived after being stabbed in a frenzied attack in New York in 2022. His assailant Hadi Matar, jailed for 25 years for the assault, praised Iran’s Ayatollah Khomeini for having called for Rushdie’s execution in the 1980s.

Sir Salman’s interview marks the launch of his new documentary – Knife, directed by Alex Gibney – about the attack, which resulted in him losing his right eye.

The film is based on his book with the same stark title. One critic called the documentary “intensely upsetting, inspiring and affecting.”

Sir Salman, who also wrote Midnight’s Children, moved to the US after spending a decade in hiding in Britain as a result of the fatwa against him issued by Iran’s Ayatollah Khomeini – partly because of the US First Amendment that pledges to uphold freedom of expression and religion.

open image in gallery A model of U.S. President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch ( Reuters )

He says Trump has made a mockery of that amendment.

“We have a brilliant liar in the White House,” he said. “It's the only thing he does well.

“The age of Trump, which includes the Biden presidency, has been a very dark time and which things have happened in America that I never believed were possible to happen.

“Attacks on our First Amendment values, free expression, hostility towards journalists and comedians. The idea that the head of the most powerful country in the world is most worried about jokes about him being told on late night television, the enormous power of the presidency that is used because of the thin skinnedness of the occupant of the of the Oval Oﬃce - it’s just horrifying.”

Sir Salman dismissed Trump’s offer to give all American adults $5,000 if the Republicans win the mid term elections in November.

“One of the things we know about Mr Trump is that he never keeps his promises, and he stiﬀs people all the time. So if anybody is foolish enough to vote for him because they think they're going to get $5,000 – it will never show up.”

Sir Salman said he believed the mid term elections will show Americans are turning against Trump, including his own hitherto fanatical Maga supporters.

“I feel there's a change in the wind. I think there's a lot of people, even from the cult that he created around himself who are beginning to be disillusioned. And we're going to find out… in the midterm elections.”

open image in gallery Sir Salman with his wife, the poet and photographer Rachel Eliza Griffiths ( Getty )

In his wide ranging interview, Sir Salman also opened his heart about falling in love with fifth wife, American poet and photographer Rachel Eliza Griffiths, nearly 30 years his junior, in a “cute” Hollywood-style chance encounter when he walked into a plate glass door.

He said some of the senior police tasked with guarding him in Britain after the 1989 Iranian fatwa were “reluctant” to protect him – partly through “racism.”

He described why it is harder now to be an immigrant in modern Britain than when he arrived here as a child – and why he still holds a grudge against one of Margaret Thatcher’s Tory ministers for accusing him of likening the UK to Nazi Germany.

And he explained why he has never read the book claimed by many to be the greatest English classic novel, George Eliot’s Middlemarch.

Recalling his ten years under police protection in the UK in the 1990s, Sir Salman said: “The people actually doing the protection, the police officers who were with me were always very sympathetic and professional, many became long term friends. The problems were at higher echelons of command, where you felt they were doing the protection reluctantly.”

Asked if that was the result of racism, his opposition to Margaret Thatcher’s government or over stretched police resources, he replied: “All of the above.

“This was the height of the Thatcher government. It was well known that I wasn't a supporter of the administration. To be fair, Margaret Thatcher authorised and kept going the protection for a long time. But that was the extent of her support. There were members of her senior members of her cabinet who said very hostile things about me, some of which were not true.

“For example, Sir Geoﬀrey Howe [Thatcher’s foreign secretary] said my novel [Satanic Verses] compared Britain to Hitler's Germany – which it does not. That was the kind of thing that was being put out there. A kind of self was being created for me, which wasn't very likeable. And a lot of people fell for that.”

Sir Salman, 79, who was born in India to non-practising Muslims and is an atheist, moved to Britain aged 13 when he attended Rugby School. He defended the role of immigrants in modern Britain.

open image in gallery The author says “the age of Trump” has been a dark time but is coming to an end ( AFP/Getty )

“It’s harder to be an immigrant today. There is a whole political rhetoric against immigrants as if they are the problem. Whereas actually, the country cannot run its hospitals or harvest its fruit or do a whole range of things that are done by immigrants.

“I've always believed that immigration is a net gain for a society.”

He deplores the large scale deportations of immigrants enforced by Trump and echoed by the likes of Nigel Farage.

“The world is international now,” he said. The idea that “somehow you can shut the door and be happy in your own little corner and not allow the world in” was absurd.

“Every country has the right to control who comes in. But in my lifetime immigrant communities have enormously enriched this country. More chicken tikka masala is eaten than roast beef and Yorkshire puddings.

“The Indian community is not a drain on the country's resources: it is a contributor.”

Sir Salman recounted the bizarre manner in which he met Rachel Eliza, who played a key role in making his new film, at a literary festival in America ten years ago.

“There was an after party on the roof terrace of a hotel. I said, ‘let's go out and look at the city at night’. It was not a chat-up line – but it wasn’t entirely not a chat-up line. There were these sliding glass doors… I didn't realise that the one on the left wasn't open. And I smashed into it… I told her that she literally knocked me out.

“I went down to get a taxi home and she was worried whether I was OK. So she came down to make sure that I got into a taxi. Then she got into the taxi. And that was that. They call it a Hollywood meeting - cute.”

Sir Salman reflected: “It has made the last decade of my life very rich. To find that level of love relatively late in life, you are very lucky. It is blind luck. Love comes at you when you're not looking for it. It whacks you over the back of the head – or in my case, the nose!”

As well as writing every day, he is a voracious reader, but confesses to never having completed Middlemarch.

“Middlemarch has been my biggest problem. I have tried to read it a number of times, I’ve got halfway, but I get bored.”

Unlikely though it may seem Booker Prize winning author Sir Salman attributes camp 1970s and 1980s British TV comedian Dick Emery for one of his first creative triumphs.

At the time struggling young author Sir Salman was working for the Ogilvy & Mather advertising agency tasked with coming up with catchy slogans. He dreamed up “naughty but nice” to sell fresh cream cakes.

He remembers his bosses’ initial expression of horror. “They said ‘you're telling people that cream cakes made them fat’. I said ‘they know that’.

“Dick Emery had this slogan at the time. ‘You are awful. But I like you.’ It was a variation of that theme.”

News.title: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation
News.content:
Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”

News.title: Red Roses triumph over New Zealand in chaotic late scenes – how it unfolded
News.content:
Just when it looked like the Red Roses’ lustre was beginning to fade, up stepped Zoe Harrison.

In one of the most dramatic finishes to an England match in recent memory, the fly-half gobbled up Amy Du Plessis’s pass to glide over the whitewash and secure a pulsating win over New Zealand.

Ever the epitome of calmness, Harrison was undeterred by the fact she had just missed what would have been a match-winning penalty from 42 metres out with the score locked at 19-19.

But after their arm-wrestle with Canada last weekend in Exeter, which finished 26-26, there was simply no way the Red Roses were going to settle for a draw for a second week running.

A year to the day since they were crowned world champions in their own back yard, England’s status as the most dominant side in the women’s game was all but confirmed by this never-say-die victory over the Black Ferns.

News.title: Russell holds his nerve to see off Verstappen and win Azerbaijan GP
News.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.

Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.

Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.

The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

News.title: Scotland’s Pocognoli era starts with encouraging signs but familiar issues in front of goal
News.content:
Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

News.title: Carreras’ try-of-season contender helps Bath eclipse Harlequins
News.content:
And they kept playing, it was not until Richards scored in the 72nd minute that the game was decided. Still for Bath, a five-try victory away from home, felt like a decent return.

If they were to stand any chance of finding a way back into the game, Quins had to score first after the restart. They were rewarded for their attacking intent after running from a scrum deep in their half, with Murley cutting a brilliant line before Pedro Delgado drove over for his side’s third try.

Quins had the opportunity to further cut the deficit when first Sam Riley carried down the left wing and Cameron Anderson drove into the Bath 22. But as Quins looked to pick and go, Beno Obano and Guy Pepper combined to hold the ball up over the line.

It felt like a significant moment and when Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Obano moments later, the odds against a Quins comeback lengthened again. Yet there was something sticky about their resilience.

“I am really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half,” said Gilmore. “We had some massive defensive sets on our goal-line which we withstood. I reckon they were the moments last year that Bath would probably run in three tries really quickly and kick the score out, which is good.”

Bath emptied their bench, including the introduction of England flanker Pepper, but they could not pull away as expected in the final quarter, despite some impressive contributions by Tom de Glanville.

It was left to their line-out maul to score their first points of the second half, with Richards touching down to seal Harlequins’ fate. Still, there were enough promising glimpses to give Harlequins supporters hope that more encouraging days lie ahead.

News.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges
News.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

Of the 115 charges:

Fifty-four were for failing to provide accurate financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18

Fourteen were for failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from the same period

Five were for failing to comply with Uefa’s rules from 2013-14 to 2017-18

Seven were for breaching Premier League profitability and sustainability rules from 2015-16 to 2017-18

Thirty-five were for failing to co-operate with the investigation from 2018-23.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

Case is far from being resolved

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

News.title: This quiet Dyson fan proved itself during a heatwave
News.content:
What is the Dyson Purifier Cool PC1?

The Dyson Purifier Cool PC1 is one of the brand’s more straightforward fans. There’s no humidifying or heating here, just a focus on cooling and air purification.

True to Dyson’s design ethos, the Purifier Cool PC1 is bladeless, which makes it safe around kids and pets, and easy to clean. The tower fan uses the company’s renowned technology to project a smooth stream of air, with 10 speed settings and a 350-degree oscillation range that circulates air evenly throughout the room. It’s relatively compact and lightweight, too.

The remote control magnetically attaches to the top of the fan but you can also control the device using the MyDyson companion app.

While it doesn’t offer all the extras of Dyson’s more expensive air purifiers, it’s a solid option if you want reliable cooling without any fuss, which is why it’s our Best Buy Dyson fan.

JUMP TO:

I’ve been testing the Dyson Purifier Cool PC1 in my home office, a small-to-medium-sized room that felt more like a sauna than a workplace during the recent heatwaves. While I wasn’t precisely measuring its air purification qualities (you can find that review on our best Dyson fan round-up), the windows open onto a main road so I was able to test out its ability to handle a steady stream of traffic fumes, dust and general pollution drifting in.

I used the fan over several weeks to see how it performs on a day-to-day basis, assessing all of the usual metrics: how well it cools the room, how quiet it is during use, how intuitive the controls are and whether the design fits into a regular living or working space. And finally, as Dyson is known for its premium pricing, is the Purifier Cool PC1 worth the outlay?

News.title: Britain sends team to South Sudan as country braces for Ebola
News.content:
British Ebola specialists have been deployed to South Sudan because of fears the haemorrhagic fever will spread from neighbouring Congo.

A rare form of Ebola, known as the Bundibugyo species, is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 7,800 people have caught the virus since May, 3,700 of whom have died.

To prepare for the threat of imported cases, Britain has positioned three experts in and around the South Sudanese capital, Juba. They will assist and train local authorities on infection control, set up awareness campaigns for local communities, and test people crossing the border for the virus.

The team is employed by the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) Public Health Rapid Support Team (PHRST), which is regularly sent to the epicentre of disease outbreaks overseas – for instant the cruise ship at the centre of a deadly hantavirus in the South Atlantic earlier this year.

The current Ebola outbreak is the fastest-growing ever recorded and is on course to become the largest in history, overtaking the 2014-16 West Africa Ebola outbreak, in which around 30,000 people contracted the haemorrhagic fever and roughly a third died.

Experts fear it is only a matter of time before the virus spreads to South Sudan, which shares a 500-mile border with the DRC. Thousands of people cross the frontier each day to work, attend school and trade goods, mostly fish, in lucrative markets between the two countries.

If the virus gained a foothold in South Sudan, which became the newest country on earth after severing ties with Khartoum in 2011, experts fear the consequences would be catastrophic and worsen an already dire humanitarian situation.

“It’s so variable as to where the outbreak is spreading at the moment, there are cases from some of the border towns [with South Sudan],” Ed Newman, director of the PHRST, told The Telegraph.

“There’s a feeling [Ebola could spread] any day. Maybe you could say we’ve been lucky so far,” Mr Newman said, on the sidelines of a UKHSA conference in Manchester.

Sports.title: From Arsenal freeze & World Cup snub to future of England midfield… Lewis-Skelly proves huge point to Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Next

IT has been a hell of a four months for Myles Lewis-Skelly – and he did not even go to the World Cup.

The Arsenal star only made his first start in midfield in the Premier League for his boyhood club in May.



Fast forward to Saturday night and the 20-year-old was starting in the middle of the park for his country against the world champions.

With club-mate Declan Rice pulling out of the squad due to fitness, Lewis-Skelly was given the nod over Alex Scott to start alongside Elliot Anderson.



He made a nervy start against the mighty Spain, but who didn’t in the England side?

After that, though, like the rest of the team, he grew into the game and did not look out of place at all against the best international outfit on the planet.

It marks a stunning turnaround for the Londoner who was out of the picture under Mikel Arteta for much of the last season.

Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie were preferred to the then-teenager at left-back, while a start in his natural role of central midfield looked a world away.

A summer sale seemed a genuine possibility when he was frozen out mid-season.

But with Martin Zubimendi running on fumes as Arsenal looked to close out their first title in 22 years, Lewis-Skelly was brought back in from the cold.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He had been training in midfield for a few months, having been a No6 and a No8 in the Gunners’ academy, and started there in a 3-0 home win over Fulham on May 2.

Since then, he has not looked back.

Lewis-Skelly was superb in the Champions League semi-final victory over Atletico Madrid and impressed in the final too, which Paris Saint-Germain won on penalties.

It came a little too late to make the plane for the World Cup but Thomas Tuchel has always liked the youngster.

Playing at left-back, Lewis-Skelly scored the first goal of the Tuchel era in a 2-0 win over Albania in March 2025.



So it was no surprise to see the German bring the versatile midfielder straight back into his squad after his electric start to the Premier League season.

Zubimendi has had to get used to watching on from the bench as Lewis-Skelly struts his stuff in midfield.

And the Spaniard did again here as he was named among the substitutes for Luis de la Fuente’s reigning Euros and World Cup winners.



Lewis-Skelly’s first major contribution was a jittery pass straight to Marc Cucurella who drove into the box and saw an effort deflected out for a corner.

It was not the Arsenal man’s finest moment but was in keeping with a number of first-half errors from England involving Elliot Anderson, Jarell Quansah and, of course, Marc Guehi, who was terribly at fault for Lamine Yamal’s opener.

Lewis-Skelly shook off the early gaffe and started to assert his authority in midfield, telling team-mates where he wanted the ball and taking it in difficult positions.

He would drop back between the two centre-halves at times, to create a back three, and when Spain had goal-kicks, push forward to man-mark Rodri.

His standout moment in the first half was a drive forward, shrugging off 2024 Ballon D’Or winner Rodri and haring into the box, where he was correctly denied a penalty when going down under Pau Cubarsi pressure.



But Lewis-Skelly did look like he did not know what to do when Ballon D’Or contender for this year, Yamal, ran at him outside the box just before the break.

After the interval, MLS grew in confidence further, taking down one high ball with some tip-top chest control and almost grabbing an assist when playing through Bukayo Saka, who was denied by a last-gasp tackle.

His eyes lit up just before coming off for James Garner as he tried his luck from outside the box, but it was right down Unai Simon’s throat.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Playing Spain and their stellar, tiki-taka midfield is about as tough a test as it gets.

This was not an A+ performance but Lewis-Skelly did more than enough to pass the exam.

Sports.title: Major update in probe into £300k jewellery heist at Harry Redknapp’s £5million mansion
Sports.content:
Next

A PROBE into a £300,000 jewellery heist at Harry Redknapp’s £5million mansion has ended, with no arrests.

The ex-Premier League boss’s home was targeted by a gang while the 79-year-old was visiting wife Sandra in hospital.



It was for sale at the time and one ­theory is the gang noted details on the Rightmove listing for the property, near Dorset beach resort Sandbanks.

Items taken included a £55,000 diamond heart-shaped pendant and a £42,000 Cartier bracelet.



But detectives have now ended the investigation into the burglary, in July last year, with no arrests being made.

A spokesperson for Dorset Police said: “Our investigation has concluded.

“However, should any new lines of enquiry emerge they will be investigated accordingly.”

Redknapp managed at Soccer Aid earlier this year, and also appeared on I’m A Celebrity.

He also offered to take over as Tottenham manager at the end of last season.

Last week The Sun on Sunday revealed cops had ended an investigation into a burglary at the home Ruben Dias shared with Maya Jama.

Sports.title: ‘Turned him into traffic cone’ – Fans stunned as Dani Olmo ‘cooks’ Elliot Anderson with simple skill in England vs Spain
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY’S £116million signing Elliot Anderson was left red-faced during England’s dramatic loss to Spain in the Nations League BY Dani Olmo.

The world champions came from behind – after surrendering their lead – to pick up a 3-2 win over the Three Lions in a rematch of their Euro 2024 final at Wembley.



The European champions dominated the first few minutes in London after Lamine Yamal took advantage of Marc Guehi’s disastrous error at the back and opened the scoring just two minutes after kick-off.

The Furia Roja’s dominance was illustrated by a brilliant run from Olmo, 28, just after the 20th minute when he led a dangerous counter-attack.



And in doing so, the Barcelona star flicked the ball past Anderson, 23, who was left frozen after that simple piece of skill while his opponent sprinted towards the hosts’ half.

England fans were left gobsmacked as they watched the playmaker run past the Man City midfielder like he wasn’t even there.

One supporter tweeted: “Olmo puts on a Spain shirt and suddenly has the burst and drive to turn Elliott Anderson into a traffic cone. what an odd player!”

Another commented: “DANI OLMO JUST ENDED ELLIOT ANDERSON HERE!”

A third wrote: “Olmo just sent Elliot Anderson to Manchester.”

This fan said: “He sucked the soul out of Anderson.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That one added: “Dani Olmo finished Anderson.”

And a comment read: “He just made Anderson look foolish.”

Olmo proved to be pivotal for Spain, who saw second-half subs Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal sealing an impressive win following goals by Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane that cancelled out Yamal’s opener.

Sports.title: Andy Carroll reveals he’s been inundated with support from male sex assault victims after opening up about his ordeal
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTBALLER Andy Carroll says he has been inundated with messages of support from male sex assault victims after telling of his own ordeal.

The former England striker, 37, said many had been in touch about their own experiences since he revealed his torment in autobiography Owning It.



And he looked relaxed yesterday as he arrived to play for non-league Dagenham & Redbridge, a club he co-owns, in a 1-0 win over Hampton & Richmond Borough.

In his book, ex-Premier League star Carroll said he was sexually assaulted while sleeping in 2021 during his second stint with Newcastle United by a “celebrity mate”, a friend of his former partner who was away at the time.



The man was convicted at what Carroll described as “humiliating and horrendous trial”.

He was jailed for three years, put on the sex offender register and banned from the village Carroll lives in.

As a sexual assault victim, Carroll had automatic anonymity and only decided to detail the incident in his book “at the last minute” after chats with present girlfriend Lou Teasdale, 42.

He wrote online: “It’s been incredibly hard for me to speak about what happened. I’m still navigating what I feel comfortable sharing publicly.

“Since speaking out, so many men have messaged me about their own experiences.

“That has been incredibly powerful and has reminded me just how important it is that men feel able to talk when they’re ready.”



The book describes how Carroll’s attacker invited himself into his home to watch a boxing match.

He said he went to bed after feeling light-headed and was woken by the visitor sexually assaulting him.

Carroll ordered the man to leave and when he tried to come back in he hit him, knocking him out.



He said: “What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I’d think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football.

“The trauma of what happened to me hasn’t gone away.”

He added: “Scary to talk about but it’s made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff.

“And if me talking about it helps just one ­person, then good. It will have been worth it.”

Sports.title: England player ratings: Bellingham bosses midfield as Gordon shows his worth to Tuchel but Guehi unsteady & gifts goal
Sports.content:
Next

MAYBE we wouldn’t have beaten them in the World Cup final after all…

Spain capitalised on England’s shoddy defence to come back from 2-1 down after Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane had got the Three Lions into the lead with a comeback of our own.



Lamine Yamal opened the scoring, with the third fastest goal that the Three Lions have ever conceded at Wembley, inside one minute with Marc Guehi caught napping on the ball.

Some Anthony Gordon magic saw the LaLiga boys set this game alight, before Harry Kane scored England’s second in four minutes to see the hosts go ahead. Unfortunately though it was downhill from there…



Kane embraced his inner John Terry and slipped on the penalty spot, watching his effort crash against the crossbar from 12 yards out, before Alex Baena and old enemy Mikel Oyarzabal added two Spanish goals to slay the Three Lions.

This is how SunSport’s England reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the Three Lions:

JAMES TRAFFORD – 5

His passing out from the back was good, but his shot stopping left something to be desired as he conceded three goals and only made two saves.

Jordan Pickford’s time between the sticks might not be over just yet, but Trafford does still show plenty of promise to be England’s future number one.



JARELL QUANSAH – 5

Came incredibly close to finding England a third goal but his headed effort was just over the bar early on in the second half.

He then lashed a shot at the face of Marc Cucurella, which the home fans enjoyed, but would’ve preferred if he found the back of the net. Defensively he was fine, but not troubled as much as Nico O’Reilly on the other side.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

EZRI KONSA – 4

He didn’t really seem very involved defensively for most of the game, so it’s hard to judge him in that sense.

He made less defensive contributions than any other England defender, but also didn’t make a huge mistake like Marc Guehi next to him.



MARC GUEHI – 3

An awful mistake early on saw him give possession away to Lamine Yamal, who made no mistake in beating James Trafford from close range to score the third quickest goal England have ever conceded at Wembley Stadium.

Was booked in the second half and struggled generally tonight throughout – a good defender who had a poor game. Perhaps a potential relegation is playing on his mind….

NICO O’REILLY – 6

Had one of, if not the toughest tasks of the night in defending against Lamine Yamal, but did so reasonably well.



Yamal, of course, was always a threat but O’Reilly made his danger known too with a beautifully stood-up cross that Harry Kane headed home to give England the lead.

His poor pass backwards was straight into the feet of Dani Olmo, who set up Alex Baena for Spain to make it 2-2.

ELLIOT ANDERSON – 6

Not at his sharpest in the first half, and almost gave Spain a second goal but for the intermittent finishing ability of Ferran Torres.

But to give him some credit he was one of the few players always looking to play the ball forwards.

He was vital in England getting level, capitalising on a Nico Williams slip to slide the ball into Anthony Gordon, and improved tenfold after that.



MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 6

It’s a credit to him that he didn’t look out of place against one of the best midfields in world football.

The youngster was smooth on the ball in midfield and found some good forward passes with Elliot Anderson next to him breaking up play.

His versaility also worked really nicely for England as he could slot into the left-back role when Nico O’Reilly ventured forwards.

BUKAYO SAKA – 5

Bukayo Saka vs Marc Cucurella is always a great matchup, and you never know who is going to come out on top between them.

It was an even one in this game, with both of them keeping the other fairly quiet aside from a few clever Saka moments with the ball. Nonetheless, the was the quietest attacker in the England side.



JUDE BELLINGHAM – 8

Showed top-level composure in the middle of the park to provide a perfectly-weighted through ball to Anthony Gordon for his equaliser, and won a penalty that should’ve seen England bag a third.

He was tenacious as ever in the middle of the pitch, did his defensive duties well and is a real leader – his second half really showed how technically brilliant he is too. I can’t believe there was ever a debate about him being in the side.

ANTHONY GORDON – 8

Absolutely brilliant.



His performance overall was as sharp and decisive as the imaginary sniper celebration that followed his equalizing goal.

That goal was a special one, with a neat flick into Bellingham starting it, and a composed finish to end it – he looks extremely confident and was always looking to make something happen with his electric pace on the wing.

HARRY KANE – 7

If this game was the battle for the Ballon d’Or between Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane then the latter still deserves to win it on October 26.



It was exactly what we’ve come to expect from the England No9 – a crucial goal, with good hold-up play and the ability to drop deep and create too.

He unfortunately slipped on the Wembley turf to see a penalty crash off of the crossbar in the second half, but was still very good overall.

SUBS:

MORGAN ROGERS (ANTHONY GORDON, 70) – 5

Struggled to get involved on the left side as much as Anthony Gordon did, with Spain in the ascendancy when he came on.

JAMES GARNER (MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY, 70) – 5

Not as progressive as Myles Lewis-Skelly before him, but turned possession over nicely.

DOMINIC CALVERT-LEWIN (HARRY KANE, 82) – N/A

Hardly involved after being introduced late as England looked for a leveller.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

MORGAN GIBBS-WHITE (BUKAYO SAKA, 82) – N/A

Hardly involved after being introduced late as England looked for a leveller.

JARROD BRANTHWAITE (MARC GUEHI, 87) – N/A

Sports.title: England 2 Spain 3: Guehi howler & Kane penalty miss come back to haunt Three Lions as ruthless world champs win opener
Sports.content:
Next

THOMAS TUCHEL accepts he must now “embrace the chaos” as England manager. And here was the compelling proof why he has absolutely no choice.

Against the world champions, the Three Lions were disorganised defensively but full of pace and purpose in attack.



Ultimately, it was not good enough. Not against the very best.

The match-winner was substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who has a bit of history with England as he was the man who grabbed the clincher in the Euro 2024 final.



So after another breathless England display, which had fans tearing their hair out and cheering with delight in equal measure, it feels as though this country is far, far away as they have ever been from winning a major tournament.

Lamine Yamal scored the third quickest goal England have ever conceded at Wembley Stadium, in the second minute.



England should have been 4-0 down, maybe even 5-0, before Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane both struck and it was ludicrous that England led 2-1 at half-time.

Kane missed from the penalty spot, slipping like he did in the 2022 World Cup quarter-final against France.

Sub Alex Baena then levelled before Oyarzabal took advantage of yet more rubbish England defending.

This was the youngest team Tuchel has fielded, average age 25 years and six days, but that is no excuse for such basic errors.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

This was a typical Premier League-style performance from England and there lies the problem.

The team might have courage and spirit but it cannot keep possession or avoid kamikaze defending.

The last time England were involved in a game quite so mad was the previous match, the 6-4 win over France in the World Cup third-place play-off.

This Nations League game clearly was more important for England but Spain still won and deservedly so. It could have been embarrassing.



So even had Tuchel’s team not blown it against Argentina in the semi-final, an appearance in the final against this fabulous Spanish team would have been messy.

Manchester City’s Marc Guehi, Elliot Anderson and Nico O’Reilly were all guilty of making some really bad errors at the back and anyone would think someone was bothering them.

They were not the only culprits, however.



Forget the fact that England qualified for the World Cup without conceding a goal, the defence is nowhere near as good as some think.

England conceded eight times even before playing France in Miami underlined that there are issues that manager Tuchel has to solve, going into Euro 2028.

Jordan Pickford did not always cover himself in glory in the summer and this is surely the reason why Tuchel has given James Trafford a two-game trial.

This was Trafford’s third senior appearance and he will also face the Czech Republic on Tuesday before Pickford picks up cap no 92 against Croatia next Saturday.



Yet although he made one crucial save, Trafford was repeatedly left exposed by his team-mates in that extraordinary first half

Yamal scored after just 106 seconds via the post after he picked the pocket of Guehi who was caught dithering.

World Cup final hero Ferran Torres thought he had scored but was offside and was then left unmarked after receiving a pass from Yamal but Trafford delivered a good block.

Embarrassingly, in almost a repeat move although Rodri delivered the pass, Torres was through but slipped the ball past Trafford but wide.

And Dani Olmo also fired wide after a sensational flick from Yamal although a minute later, it was the boy wonder’s Barcelona team-mate Gordon who levelled.



Nico Williams lost the ball to Anderson, Jude Bellingham drove forward and released Gordon who took one touch before dispatching the ball underneath Unai Simon.

Although Kane made a mess of one chance by getting the ball stuck under his feet before curling a shot wide, he grabbed goal no 86 for England a few seconds later.

He needed some help from Cucurella, who diverted a stooping header into the net with his thigh following a clever cross from O’Reilly.



It should have been 3-1 after England were awarded a penalty after VAR spotted Rodri’s foul on Jude Bellingham but Kane ended up slamming his spot-kick against the bar.

Yet at no stage did England ever look like to stop Spain from scoring again. O’Reilly gave the ball away again and five minutes after arriving as a sub, Baena curled a shot past Trafford.

Baena then turned provider and found Oyarzabal who, completely unmarked, dinked the ball over the advancing Trafford.

England could have made it 3-3 and Bellingham forced a good save from Simon at the end.

So, after heartbreak at the World Cup, England failed to bring any sort of feel-good factor back to the country.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tuchel certainly made mistakes against Argentina but ultimately, it was not just his fault, like it was not always Gareth Southgate’s.

When it really matters, England are still not good enough.

Sports.title: Brazil football legend 'lost 99%' of career earnings as warning sent to young players
Sports.content:
Brazil football legend 'lost 99%' of career earnings as warning sent to young players

The former left-back has opened up about 'mistakes' he made, which had big financial consequences

View 2 Images Roberto Carlos has claimed that he lost 99% of his career earnings. (Image: Clive Rose/Getty Images)

Legendary Brazilian left-back Roberto Carlos has revealed that he lost ‘99%’ of the earnings he made throughout his career. The former Real Madrid defender is estimated to have earned around €160 million (£137.6m) throughout his playing career.

‌



He is known as one of the best ever in his position, helping Brazil to win the World Cup in 2002. He also lifted the Champions League trophy three times with Real Madrid.

‌



Despite success on the pitch, the 53-year-old has admitted to ‘mistakes’ off it, which led to him losing a lot of money. He says it’s a warning for younger players.

‌



Thomas Tuchel brutally shuts down England question live on ITV with blunt answer READ MORE :

Manchester City apology demanded after Premier League charges verdict READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Speaking at the Portugal Football Summit, Carlos said: “I had problems with people who emptied my bank account. I lost 99% of everything I earned from football.”

He added: "I had a very serious family problem. On Thursday, I went to bed at midnight and on Friday, I received a pile of documents I knew nothing about. That’s when I realised I had lost my entire history.

‌



“I made mistakes, and therefore, I ask younger players not to do the same. I always thought about future plans after my playing career.

“It’s about building a history as a player and leveraging your image. When I decided to leave football, I already had my sporting director’s licence and was working with many brands.”

Carlos played 817 games for seven different clubs throughout a 20-plus-year career. He appeared to retire in 2012, but made a comeback in 2015, signing for Indian side Delhi Dynamos.

‌



View 2 Images Brazil legend Roberto Carlos during a legends match in 2022 (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire.)

He made just three appearances in the Indian Super League before announcing his retirement in 2016. He now works as a club representative for Real Madrid and is the owner of Brazilian third-tier side AA Internacional de Limeira, and was over in America for the summer's World Cup.

The former left-back underwent planned surgery last year, and moved to confirm that he did not suffer a heart attack. "I would like to clarify recent information that has been circling. I recently underwent a preventative medical procedure, planned in advance with my medical team," he wrote on Instagram.

Article continues below

"The procedure was successful, and I am well. I did not suffer a heart attack. I am recovering well, and looking forward to returning to full fitness and resuming my professional and personal commitments soon.

"I sincerely thank everyone for messages of support, care, and concern."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Jurgen Klopp player could be re-signed as Reds weigh up £47m decision
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Jurgen Klopp player could be re-signed as Reds weigh up £47m decision

Liverpool round-up as the Reds weigh up several transfer calls

View 3 Images Jurgen Klopp talking to Liverpool players including Tyler Morton (right) (Image: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola has plenty of food for thought following a solid, if unspectacular, start to his Liverpool reign. The Reds sit sixth in the table after five games, six points off early leaders Manchester City, who could potentially be hit with a massive points penalty after being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League.

‌



The Reds' hard-fought win at Bournemouth suggested that Iraola has solid foundations on which to build as he looks to mastermind a title challenge and make an impact in the Champions League.

‌



There are still issues he will be mulling over between now and the Reds' next game, against City on October 11, such as an unbalanced squad and how to get the best out of Florian Wirtz, who is currently with Germany and working under Jurgen Klopp.

‌



Iraola will be hoping the 18 first-team players called up for international duty return unscathed. Here's a round-up of the latest Reds news…

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Klopp favourite could be re-signed

Liverpool are reportedly considering re-signing Wirral-born midfielder Tyler Morton. After rising through the Reds' youth ranks, Morton made his senior debut under Jurgen Klopp in 2021 before loan spells at Hull City and Blackburn Rovers.

‌



Rio Ngumoha cut from Thomas Tuchel's England squad to face Spain due to UEFA rules READ MORE :

Jurgen Klopp forced into immediate Florian Wirtz U-turn after Germany injury blow READ MORE :

While Klopp was a huge fan of the youngster, he didn't make a single Premier League appearance during Arne Slot's title-winning season and was allowed to leave for Lyon in the summer of 2025 in a deal worth £15million.

The 23-year-old has since won rave reviews in France and is attracting attention from the Reds and Juventus, according to the Tutto Juve website. The Serie A giants are in the market for an experienced young midfielder.

Meanwhile, the Reds are reportedly regretting letting Morton go and are seriously considering bringing him back to Merseyside. Morton has made 10 appearances so far this season for Lyon, who sit second in the Ligue 1 table, two points off Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



View 3 Images Tyler Morton made his Reds debut under Jurgen Klopp (Image: Getty Images)

Reds weigh up £47m call

Liverpool are already considering making Ronald Araujo's loan move permanent following an impressive start to his Anfield career. The 27-year-old has taken a pay cut to facilitate the move, for which the club have an option to buy for £47million should it prove successful.

Araujo's versatility has proved particularly useful to Iraola. After starting the season in the centre of defence, the Uruguay international switched to right-back, impressing in both roles.

‌



View 3 Images Araujo has enjoyed a bright start to life with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

According to Mundo Deportivo, the Reds are already minded to take up the non-obligation option to sign Araujo permanently next summer. If he continues his current form, £47m would represent a bargain.

It seems the player himself is open to remaining in England after reportedly buying a house near the Reds' training ground for him, his wife and his two daughters. He is also said to be having regular English lessons with a private tutor.

Sports.title: Manchester City apology demanded after Premier League charges verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester City apology demanded after Premier League charges verdict

Manchester City were found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules this week, with calls for the club to issue an apology demanded in the aftermath

View Image Manchester City have been urged to apologise (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Richard Keys has demanded that Manchester City apologise after being found guilty of breaching 114 Premier League financial rules. The Cityzens were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges that they were slapped with in 2023 on Friday.

‌



And while club chairman, Khaldoon Al Mubarak, has urged football fans not to jump to conclusions, continuing to plead innocence, others have called for immediate penalisation and punishment for the infractions. That includes long-time presenter Keys, who most recently worked for BeIN Sports.

‌



Taking to X, the 69-year-old wrote: "The bottom line is Manchester City owe English football an apology. They cheated & warped our game.

‌



Roy Keane and Ian Wright urge Premier League to punish Man City after 'cheat' verdict READ MORE :

Thomas Tuchel gives reason for surprise Jordan Pickford England decision vs Spain READ MORE :

"I know it’s nothing to do with the guys on the pitch but most of them wouldn’t have been there if City had played by the rules. Their achievements feel very hollow right now."

Given City's stance on the charges, an appeal of Friday's verdict from an independent panel is expected. As a result, any punishment will not be dished out to the Manchester team until that aspect of the case is concluded.

However, as for the possibilities, the outlook is grim for City. While lighter punishments could come in the form of fines and transfer embargoes, more extreme situations could see the club docked points, expelled from the Premier League or even have their titles won during the affected period - between 2009 and 2018 - stripped.

‌



Any decision is guaranteed to be a little while away as of yet, with fellow Premier League fans and clubs alike set for a period of uncertainty regarding City's situation. For City fans, Al Mubarak has thanked them for their consistent support en-masse.

Sports.title: Gavin Bazunu releases statement after Ireland star pulls out of Israel game
Sports.content:
Gavin Bazunu releases statement after Ireland star pulls out of Israel game

Bolton Wanderers goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu has confirmed he will not feature for the Republic of Ireland in their Nations League fixture against Israel on Sunday

View 2 Images Gavin Bazunu will not play against Israel

Gavin Bazunu has shared a statement explaining the reasons behind his decision to make himself unavailable for the Republic of Ireland's forthcoming match against Israel.

‌



The UEFA Nations League fixture, which will take place at a neutral venue in Hungary, had been cast into doubt on Saturday when Ireland delayed both their pre-match training session and press conference. It then emerged that players were considering a boycott of the fixture following calls for them to do so amid the backdrop of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

‌



A statement later confirmed that Sunday's game would take place. But Bazunu has decided against participating in the match, with the Bolton Wanderers goalkeeper condemning the ongoing conflict.

‌



He said: "Representing my country means everything to me. I have the utmost respect for every single one of my team-mates, the Manager, his staff and the Irish people.

‌



"However I have reached a decision that I have not taken lightly. I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle therefore I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel.

"My decision is based purely upon my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong.

"It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition of the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region.

‌



"There are few times where you get a chance in life to stand up for something bigger and I strongly believe that this is one of them."

View 2 Images Bazunu did not join the Republic of Ireland team for training on Saturday afternoon (Image: Getty)

A UN-commissioned inquiry previously found that Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians in war-torn Gaza. More than 73,000 people have been killed after Israeli military action was launched in response to the Hamas attack on the Nova Festival in southern Israel of October 7 2023, which killed approximately 1,200 people.

Article continues below

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) confirmed Sunday's game would go ahead following a vote between Ireland's players over whether to fulfil the fixture.

"The association made this decision following consultation with the Republic of Ireland players who shared different views and a majority expressed that the fixtures should be played," the FAI's statement read. "The association respects the views of all players involved and appreciates the level of sensitivity concerning these fixtures."

Sports.content:
Roy Keane and Ian Wright urge Premier League to punish Man City after 'cheat' verdict

Ian Wright and Roy Keane were on hand to give their opinion on Manchester City's Premier League charges guilty verdict during ITV's coverage of the Nations League

View Image Roy Keane and Ian Wright agree about Manchester City's charges (Image: ITV)

Roy Keane and Ian Wright agree that Manchester City should be severely punished for 'cheating' after being found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. Following a long and drawn-out three year saga, an independent panel found City guilty of all but one of the 115 charges slapped against them by English top flight officials on Friday evening.

‌



While City are expected to appeal the decision, given they have continually plead their innocence, the footballing world was sent into a frenzy by the earth-shattering news, with players, pundits and fans all having their say. Highlighting the extent of the controversy, Rodri spent a large portion of his Nations League press conference for Spain answering questions regarding his former club's alleged wrongdoing.

‌



And now, Premier League legends Keane and Wright have given their verdict on matters. Speaking during ITV's coverage of the Nations League clash between England and Spain at Wembley alongside Mark Pougatch and Juan Mata, Keane said: "Well it's about time [the decision was made]. It's obviously been going on a long time now and I certainly would disagree with Rodri's messages there.

‌

Jose Mourinho's dig at Pep Guardiola on Man City charges with Man Utd bonus claim READ MORE :

"It was the choice of the club, they chose to cheat, and whatever they have won over the last few years, they deserve to be punished. Where we start and finish with that, obviously it's difficult.

"But they were cheating. Been found guilty of it, they have to take their medicine now. And it was kind of a shock really to be found guilty of...114 of the charges they were found guilty of? Big news it was."

When asked where the debacle leaves the reputation of English football, Wright then added: "Not very good, not very good. I'm going to be totally honest, Pougs.

‌



"Going back to Rodri, he's talking about what he's done. He went shoulder to shoulder with the guys, and, of course, you can't take that away from them, they experienced that.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel gives reason for surprise Jordan Pickford England decision vs Spain
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel gives reason for surprise Jordan Pickford England decision vs Spain

Thomas Tuchel chose James Trafford as England's goalkeeper ahead of Jordan Pickford to face Spain

View 2 Images Jordan Pickford was named on the bench for England's clash against Spain (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

England manager Thomas Tuchel has explained the reason why he chose to start James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford for the clash against Spain. The Three Lions are facing the reigning world champions at Wembley Stadium on Saturday night in the Nations League.

‌



The clash in London is England’s first match since beating France in the bronze medal match at the World Cup, while it’s Spain’s first game since winning the final against Argentina on July 19 in New Jersey.

‌



Pickford started all of England’s matches on their way to reaching the World Cup semi-final, with Dean Henderson getting the nod for the third-fourth place play-off against France, which ended in a dramatic 6-4 victory for Tuchel’s side.

‌



Trafford starts in goal for England against Spain, with Tuchel explaining that an increase in minutes for the shot-stopper since completing a move to Leeds United in the summer transfer window played a factor in his decision.

Erling Haaland update as Norway boss explains Nations League U-turn after 115 charges READ MORE :

Jose Mourinho's dig at Pep Guardiola on Man City charges with Man Utd bonus claim READ MORE :

The England boss also went on to praise Pickford for the way the Everton goalkeeper reacted to dropping to the bench for the fixture.

"He [Trafford] gets two matches, consecutive matches, because he deserves it, and Pickers [Pickford] gets the other two matches," Tuchel told ITV ahead of kick-off at Wembley.

‌



"It was amazing to see how Jordan Pickford received the message and his reaction to it. We told him that we want to see Trafford at this kind of level in goal.

"We want to use this competition because he has a good start for Leeds, a lot of minutes, he’s starting now, that’s the difference to last season.

View 2 Images James Trafford starts for England against Spain (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"So we want to see what’s behind Pickers, we know what Pickers can give us. He did nothing wrong, and he kept pushing and was very positive about it."

As well as naming Trafford in goal, Tuchel also selected a back four that featured Jarell Quansah, Ezri Konsa, Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly.

‌



Elliott Anderson and Myles Lewis-Skelly start in midfield for England against the world champions, just behind Jude Bellingham, who also has Bukayo Saka and Anthony Gordon on the wings.

Harry Kane also started for England as the Bayern Munich star looks to add to his goal tally for his country.

But the game got off to a less-than-ideal start for Trafford, with Guehi caught in possession on the edge of his own box by Lamine Yamal, who slotted calmly past the England keeper to open the scoring after less than two minutes.

He added: "Therefore, I think it is timely that he concentrates on what he should do, and that is to score goals for Norway. And I think we all agree that that is the most important thing."

Sports.title: Wakefield hailed after stunning Wigan: 'No team would have competed!'
Sports.content:
Jon Wilkin believes some of the best teams in Super League history would not have beaten Wakefield Trinity on Saturday night, as Daryl Powell's side sealed a huge upset victory against Wigan Warriors to book a spot in the Grand Final.

A flurry of second-half tries saw Trinity end Wigan's 16-match winning streak, with the visitors leaving Matt Peet's side stunned by their ferocious pace and power.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the highlights as Wakefield produced a huge upset against Wigan

Wigan went down to 12 men after 45 minutes, with Adam Keighran being sin-binned for a tip-tackle. Wakefield ruthlessly took advantage, scoring three tries while the Australian five-eighth was off the field.

Wigan did impress in the opening exchanges, matching Wakefield for intensity, with Brad O'Neill breaking the deadlock after a tense first 15 minutes.

But the League Leaders' Shield winners, who had two weeks off coming into this match, stumbled in the second half.

"Wigan were bad, but that was completely induced by what Wakefield threw at them," Wilkin told Sky Sports.

"It was a clinical performance that was full of power, pace, energy, enthusiasm and execution.

"Nobody would have competed with Wakefield today. Not one team in Super League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Trinity scored three tries after Wigan's Adam Keighran was sent to the sin bin for a tip tackle

"I'd go as far as to say some of the great teams we've had in the history of Super League wouldn't have competed with that 80 minutes that Wakefield have dished up."

After Keighran was sent to the bin, Tom Johnston touched down in the corner with a diving finish, before Jack Sinfield beat Junior Nsemba from close range to score another.

They had a third in seven minutes, with Corey Hall sprinting down the wing before smashing his way over the tryline.

Ky Rodwell wrapped up the 27-point win, thanks to some great hands from Jake Trueman.

After the match, Peet lauded Wakefield, adding his Wigan side were "well prepared" but came up second on the night.

"Wakefield were outstandingly good," the Warriors coach said. "All the credit in the world to them, to Daryl. We were outplayed, outcoached, and beaten all ends up.

"Credit to them, it hurts, but the night belongs to them."

A new name on the Super League trophy is now guaranteed, with Trinity to face Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford next Saturday, which is live on Sky Sports.

Powell lauded as top coach

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tom Johnstone scored twice in the match

Powell left his role with Castleford Tigers at the conclusion of the 2021 Super League season, having guided the side to a Challenge Cup final appearance and their maiden Super League Grand Final.

He was appointed head coach at Wakefield in October 2023, and has been instrumental in lifting the club from the Championship to its first Super League Grand Final, after one of their best seasons on record.

"I think the jury was still out after his spell at Castleford," Wilkin said.

"But there is no doubt that Daryl Powell is an exceptional coach, who can get a group of men organised and directed to success.

"That's what he's done, and he's done it with such style and class.

"Wakefield play with risk and they play the game in a beautiful way."

Ellis: I didn't think in my wildest dreams we'd do that

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The victory continues Wakefield's remarkable 2026 season

Wakefield owner Matt Ellis heaped praise on his team following the match:

"It's still not sunk in yet. Four-and-a-half thousand fans still singing away. What a performance.

"That was the best performance in my time owning the club. So proud of them. We just nailed it today, didn't we?

"I didn't think in my wildest dreams [we'd be four scores up].

"I had a good feeling all week about it; all the pressure was on them. We came here, we were confident.

"It's a happy group, but it's an even happier group right now.

"There's so many good stories, three years after relegation, and now we're there!"

Sports.title: 'These things are never over!' - Can Team USA avoid another Medinah upset?
Sports.content:
Brandt Snedeker has given a self-critical assessment of his own Presidents Cup captaincy so far, with time quickly running out to avoid an embarrassing defeat for Team USA on home soil.

Team USA came into the week as overwhelming favourites to claim a record-extending 11th consecutive victory, in a biennial event where much of the pre-tournament narrative was around whether change was needed to make it more competitive.

Next to no hope had been given to Geoff Ogilvy's International Team, who earned their only Presidents Cup win in 1998 and have lost every edition since a 17-17 tie in 2003, but they are now five points away from completing a seismic shock at Medinah.

A clean sweep in the Friday foursomes gave the visitors a 7-3 advantage heading into Saturday's double session, where the Internationals saw the leaderboard filled with red numbers in both - indicating American leads - before delivering late fightbacks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the second day of the 2026 Presidents Cup, where the International Team impressed during the Friday foursomes

The Internationals claimed a share of the spoils in the afternoon foursomes to take a 10.5-7.5 advantage into the Sunday singles, just the fourth time they've led heading into the final day of a Presidents Cup and first experience of it on American soil.

"It's tough when there's all red on the board, but to get 2-2 out of that afternoon session and to go into tomorrow with a lead, which was the goal at the start of the week, I'm very proud of them," Ogilvy said.

Team USA have been outpointed in foursomes for a second successive Presidents Cup and have been dominated on the par-threes around Medinah, with the International Team holding a 25-6 advantage on those holes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tom Kim shushed the American crowd after holing a putt to win a hole during the Presidents Cup fourballs

Snedeker's strategy and pairings have come under scrutiny, with Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman a winless foursomes pairing in two sessions and Wyndham Clark returning just one point from his four matches so far.

Scottie Scheffler's torrid foursomes record for Team USA continued alongside Sam Burns, leading to him being benched on Saturday afternoon, with a frazzled Snedeker even getting muddled by his own selections during a live TV interview.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker forgot the name of Cameron Young, one of his players, during a live interview ahead of the Presidents Cup Saturday fourballs

"I tried to work my tail off to put these guys in the best situation possible and I don't think I've done a very good job this week, to be where we are right now," Snedeker admitted in his press conference.

"They [Team USA] look to me to put them in the best position where they're comfortable. I hold myself to a high standard - I don't think I've done the best job for them in that room.

"They've given me everything I could possibly ask for and I've just got to figure out ways to get these guys in better situations. I don't think I've held up my end of the bargain. The guys have done everything I've asked of them so far."

Another Medinah upset ahead?

It would be somewhat fitting if the Internationals could close out an elusive away victory on Sunday at Medinah, 14 years on from Team Europe producing their own unlikely success over Team USA at the same venue.

Europe's comeback from 10-4 down to win 14.5-13.5 in 2012 was miraculous enough for it to be the 'Miracle at Medinah', although their pre-tournament hopes had been far stronger that week than what was expected from the International Team here.

Three points is a far friendlier deficit to overcome than the United States faced at last year's Ryder Cup, where they briefly threatened to come back from seven behind before Europe eventually survived their scare to win 15-13.

Team USA appeared to have the pre-tournament edge in world rankings, PGA Tour success and squad depth, with Snedeker still hopeful his side can continue a winning run that has seen them claim 13 of the previous 15 editions.

"A lot can happen on these Sundays," Snedeker insisted. "We've seen it happen a lot over the last couple of years. I think we're going to draw on what happened last year at the Ryder Cup and how close we came to that big comeback.

Sports.title: Is Russell really back after Baku brilliance?
Sports.content:
George Russell produced the most statistically complete weekend of his Formula 1 career to win the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, but did the performance confirm the Brit is back to his best?

Russell drove superbly in Baku to claim the first Grand Slam of his career, taking pole position, leading from lights-to-flag on his way to victory, and setting the fastest lap of the race.

The result saw Russell reduce his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's lead at the top of the world championship to 66 points with eight rounds remaining, ensuring some intrigue remains as the season enters its closing stretch.

Regardless of whether Russell is able to mount a challenge over the remainder of the season, the gulf between him and Antonelli in recent months had begun to create doubts over the 28-year-old's prospects of ever winning a championship while driving alongside the Italian.

There were extenuating circumstances for Antonelli in Baku as he missed a significant chunk of practice with technical issues before crashing out of qualifying to leave himself 16th on the grid, but this was the first time since the opening weekend of the season that Russell had so clearly outperformed him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Russell has been open in recent months about his difficulty understanding his deficit to Antonelli, which he has largely attributed to the different challenges posed by F1's new cars for 2026, but feels his Baku display was confirmation that a corner has been turned.

Russell said: "I think it's probably my first Grand Slam in Formula 1 and, for sure, the most dominant weekend I've had in my career, so that has come at a really great moment.

"And also to achieve it on a circuit that requires so much commitment and confidence, I'm really proud of because I think it would have been very easy for me to lose the faith this season. Not necessarily about winning the championship, but in terms of my ability, and that never happened.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell describes his tense showdown with Max Verstappen for the Azerbaijan GP win.

"I'm very proud of the resilience that I and my close group of engineers have shown during the tough periods this year because there's been a lot of hard work to overcome some of the challenges, to adapt my driving style to suit this new car better.

"And F1 is so tough, you don't get opportunities to practice this, and finally it's coming to me a bit more intuitively than it once did, and I'm gaining confidence."

'He definitely stepped up'

Russell's victory was made all the more impressive by the fact he had to fend off Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the closing stages having had a big lead taken away by two Safety Car interruptions.

A thrilling race to the chequered flag saw Russell end up just a tenth of a second clear of Verstappen, creating the smallest margin of victory in an F1 race since 2002.

Three-time W Series champion and Sky Sports F1 pundit Jamie Chadwick believes the performance was confirmation that Russell has raised his level.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell holds onto the lead on the opening lap of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"He's definitely stepped up," Chadwick said.

"It's a big points gap but I think the championship is still something to be excited about, which for a lot of us coming into this weekend maybe we didn't expect. So that's something to look forward to now."

Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok was particularly impressed by the way Russell fended off four-time world champion Verstappen in the closing stages.

"That last stint from George, he had Verstappen piling the pressure on," Chandhok said. "In some ways that's more satisfying for George.

"It's one thing disappearing off, 10 seconds in the lead and driving by yourself. But winning under pressure will give him more satisfaction."

Can Russell keep it up?

If Russell really has returned to form, it was good time to do so, with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix having been the first of six races in seven weeks.

The Bahrain Grand Prix, taking place in Malaysia, follows next weekend, with the Singapore Grand Prix completing a triple-header. Then come back-to-back races in the United States, Mexico and Brazil.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok is joined by George Russell to watch back his pole-setting lap for the Azerbaijan GP.

The fact Russell needs to take a grid penalty before the end of the season for changing engine stiffens his task, but just proving that he can match Antonelli for pace over the remainder of the year would be a huge psychological boost going into 2027.

Having rarely spoken with any great confidence in recent months, Russell's view on how he sees the battle between himself and Antonelli going forward suggests he has his mojo back.

"There's much less pressure on me than there is him," Russell said. "He's had an incredibly flawless season. Yesterday was probably his first mistake of this whole season in a proper session, qualifying, race, and he still came home in P5 today.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during qualifying at the Azerbaijan GP.

"I didn't really consider myself in this fight for a number of races, purely because my performance wasn't strong enough.

"Now I feel like if the season were to have started today, or since the summer break, I feel very much I would have been able to fight.

"Now I've got this big deficit. It can change quickly. So, I'm not chasing that. I'm chasing to win every race, and what will be, will be."

Sports.title: Internationals take shock lead over USA into singles after late drama
Sports.content:
The International Team moved another step closer to a historic Presidents Cup win on American soil by taking a 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into the Sunday singles.

Geoff Ogilvy's side held a four-point advantage after the first two days at Medinah Country Club, following their historic foursomes sessions sweep on Friday, then added 1.5 points from four matches during a tight Saturday fourballs session.

Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker benched world No 1 Scottie Scheffler for the afternoon foursomes, where they threatened their own session sweep after grabbing the early lead in all four matches.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns' fourballs victory over Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune on Saturday morning

Cameron Young and Chris Gotterup thrashed Adam Scott and Sungjae Im 6&4, before Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele saw off Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim 2&1 to reduce the deficit further, only for the Internationals to fight back in an impressive finish.

Ryan Fox and Min Woo Lee bounced back from falling behind early to defeat Sam Burns and Wyndham Clark 3&2 in the bottom match, guaranteeing the Internationals would start the Sunday singles ahead for just the fourth time ever.

Snedeker reveals 'mistakes' as Internationals 'weathered the storm'

Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker:

"I thought our guys battled hard. It was a tough day out there. This golf course got really tough this afternoon. There's such a fine line between good shots and bad shots and I was proud of the way the guys hung in there and battled.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker forgot the name of Cameron Young, one of his players, during a live interview ahead of the Presidents Cup Saturday fourballs

"It's going to be a long, hard day tomorrow. I've got the right guys in that team room. They're going to compete. So proud of how they've kind of hung in there this week, despite all of my mistakes. Can't wait to see them go out there tomorrow and compete."

"What a day! They (Team USA) came out firing, as we knew they would. They were up in all four in the morning and we thought we stole a point and a half a little bit, to get out of that with only 2.5-1.5.

"This afternoon, same thing. The United States came out playing well, which we know they're going to. They're some of the best players in the world, but the boys hung tough and sort of weathered the storm if you like and started making a few putts.

Image: Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim have won three of their four matches together this week

"It's tough when there's all red on the board, but to get 2-2 out of that afternoon session and to go into tomorrow with a lead, which was the goal at the start of the week, I'm very proud of them."
