World.title: SA faces severe storms, damaging winds and extreme fire danger today
World.content:
Dark storm clouds gather as severe thunderstorms, damaging winds and extreme fire danger threaten parts of South Africa. Image: Pexels

South Africa faces a mix of severe weather today, with thunderstorms, damaging winds and extremely high fire danger conditions expected in parts of the country.

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued Yellow Level 2 warnings for severe thunderstorms over parts of KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga, while some areas of Gauteng and North West face extremely high fire danger conditions.

Severe thunderstorms threaten KZN and Mpumalanga

Severe thunderstorms could bring heavy downpours, strong damaging winds, hail and excessive lightning to most of KwaZulu-Natal, except the extreme southern parts, as well as the eastern Highveld in Mpumalanga.



The storms could flood susceptible roads, low-lying areas and bridges, while strong winds and hail could damage settlements and infrastructure.

Damaging winds could disrupt travel

SAWS has also warned of damaging interior winds across most of KwaZulu-Natal, apart from the south-western parts.

The winds could damage settlements and affect some transport routes and travel services.



Along the KwaZulu-Natal coast, strong winds and waves could disrupt small harbours and a port.

Small vessels could take on water or capsize, while rough conditions could make navigation difficult.

Extremely high fire danger in Gauteng and North West

The weather service has also warned of extremely high fire danger conditions in Ratlou and Mahikeng local municipalities in North West, as well as the northern and central parts of Gauteng.



Residents in these areas should take extra care with any activities that could start or spread a fire.

World.title: Exclusive: Bontle Modiselle on keeping her ‘Masked Singer’ secret
World.content:
South African actress and dancer Bontle Modiselle sat down with The South African for an exclusive interview on her The Masked Singer South Africa season three experience as she won the series. Bontle was under the mask of Spotty.

The Masked Singer South Africa season three finale aired on SABC 2 on Saturday 26 September.

BONTLE MODISELLE WINS MASKED SINGER SA SEASON THREE



Bontle Modiselle, known for acting and dancing, has proven that she is a triple-threat. She bagged the number one spot on The Masked Singer SA season three defeated Robot Boii (Mosquito) who came in as the runner-up, Khanyi Mbau (Chopsticks) and Judith Sephuma (Gogga).



As The Masked Singer SA was pre-recorded over a span of 13 weeks, Bontle expressed that she was sitting with her win for a while now, and now that everyone knows, she is reliving it.

“I’ve been sitting with this victory for a while now because we stopped recording some time ago. So I’m reliving it, and now everyone finding out is exciting, it really is,” she said.

KEEPING THE BIG SECRET

The Masked Singer franchise is known for their high-level of secrecy in concealing the identities of the celebrities under the masks. Bontle expressed that keeping the secret was very difficult, especially from her mom who lives with her and her helper. While she did have to tell her husband. Bontle is married to Ricardo Moloi, popularly known as Priddy Ugly.

“Keeping the secret was incredibly hard. My mom lives with me and my husband and we have a helper, so needing to keep the secret from them was unreal. The only person in the house who knew was my husband because of how we had to leave the house, in a visor, completely covered up. You know being picked up, being dropped off was hard. So I had to fill him in and say ‘okay husband, no trust issues between us, this is what’s happening.’ So Rose and Oaks, Anele (Mdoda) and Frankie (du Toit) I think they understood how isolating an experience like this can be, but they knew how to make it the most high-profile, premium experience,” she said.

“So, it didn’t feel bad… at all. It was incredibly beautiful, it felt premium, you know you’re being picked up in this stunning car, and then you’ve got this security that’s on stand by waiting for you… and lockdown as soon as you step into the building, get into the green room and you have an entire buffet of things you like to eat waiting for you. You get into your rehersals, you bang it out, you do your things. They respected our time, they respected our effort,” she continued.

BONTLE MODISELLE ON GAINING CONFIDENCE IN HER SINGING THROUGH ‘THE MASKED SINGER SA’

The actress, who has 4.2 million followers on Instagram, expressed that she had fun recording and gave credit to South African singer-songwriter and musician Khaya Mthethwa.



“When it came to the recording of the song, it was so much fun. We had one studio session and we banged out all the songs, all at once. So, that was fun, Khaya Mthethwa was absolutely brilliant. Every insecurity went out the window. He really guided us through every note, through every vocal, through every lyric. He was very patient with us. It was an unreal experience from beginning to end,” she said.

She also expressed that she was excited to be under the mask of Spotty.

“It was two things: I was excited, but also it was like ‘oh no it’s me, and now you guys know’. There was something about individuality that was interesting because you’re excited to be revealed. But you also come to the reality that it has come to an end, but it was magical. Absolutely magical,”

Bontle further explained that the best part of being on the show was her performance as Spotty.

“Being Spotty and just doing what I wanted to do and just being on that stage was so much fun. You know when you have a dream… and it’s a thing you haven’t done and you finally get to do it? And I got to do it through this character of Spotty. My favourite part was getting into studio and recording, because I was like I always wanted to be in front of the mic. I’m no stranger to the mic, my husband makes music and we’ve made music before. But I didn’t have the confidence to fully pursue it,” she continued.

She teased that she could be venturing into the music industry as an artist herself now. Bontle also expressed that she was previously afraid to be judged over her voice.

“I think the vulnerability of being heard and being judged kept me from singing before. I think I just needed to get over being judged, through the thing that I felt the most afraid about… there’s just things I’ve been scared to do when singing is concerned, I always questioned my level of confidence in it,” she said.

“And it’s a raw vocal, it’s not being tweaked, it’s not being manipulated in any way. How I was on the show is how I sound. And we know that people can mix and engineer all of that to enhance what people sound like. Now, people know what I sound like, now I know I can do it. Do not be afraid if I drop music,” she said.

Bontle added that from all the songs she performed Titanium was by far her favourite followed by Drive. Spotty performed Drive alongside runner-up Robot Boii, who was under the mask of Mosquito.

“That song just affirmed that ‘you actually got some chops, there’s something we can do with it’ but Drive was so many things. It was vocal and it was performance and it was a performance next to a contender, who I absolutely respected. He (Robot Boii) was one of my favourites on the show, and he is in my personal space and world. We work very well together,” she said.

World.title: LIVE SCORING: Springboks v Wallabies in Perth
World.content:
A new-look Springbok team will have an opportunity to once again demonstrate the incredible depth available to Rassie Erasmus as a ‘second side’ looks to claim victory over the Wallabies.

Erasmus made 13 changes to his starting team, with only lock Eben Etzebeth and wing Ethan Hooker retaining their places in the run-on team from the side’s last 43-28 victory against the All Blacks in Baltimore.

It does present a huge opportunity for several players who will receive some much needed game-time and look to make an impression before the end-of-year tour.



“We are excited about the guys getting an opportunity after a tough four weeks against the All Blacks (in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series), especially guys such as Canan Moodie and Handre Pollard, who were close to playing in one of the games and then got injured,” said assistant coach Mzwandile Stick.

“I’m also thrilled to see a guy like Herschel Jantjies. He’s probably only played about 25 minutes this season, but he’s been great in training sessions, so I’m very excited for him to get a chance.

“We always want to build squad depth. Obviously, the goal was slightly different when it came to the series against the All Blacks, because we treated it more like playoffs or a Rugby World Cup scenario.



“But this game against Australia gives us an opportunity to give other guys a chance to see what they’ve got. They have worked very hard to be where they are and they deserve the opportunity, so hopefully tomorrow can also be a good game.”

The match at the Optus Stadium kicks off at 11:45 (SA time) and will be broadcast live on SuperSport.

World.title: Ekurhuleni Murders | Suspect arrested following discovery of woman's body in Thembisa
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – A suspect was arrested in Limpopo for allegedly being involved in the killing of a woman whose body was found at the Mooifontein Cemetery in Thembisa south.

Police said the suspect allegedly fled to Tzaneen after the murder.

Acting National Commissioner of the South African Police Service (SAPS), Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane, has commended Gauteng police for the swift apprehension of a suspect.

“I commend this multidisciplinary team for their swift response, coordination and determination, which resulted in the apprehension of the suspect on the same day. This is the kind of policing we expect from our members. We will continue to pursue perpetrators of murder and gender-based violence and femicide and ensure that they face the full might of the law,” said Dimpane.

Police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said the investigation and tracing of perpetrators linked to other women's bodies found in Ekurhuleni is still underway with police following all available leads.

World.title: 17 killed in West Rand tavern shooting
World.content:
CARLETONVILLE - Police have launched a manhunt for eight armed suspects after a deadly tavern shooting in Wedela township near Carletonville.

17 people including 13 men and four women, were killed when the gunmen opened fire on patrons inside and outside the tavern on Saturday night.

More than a dozen were wounded and taken to hospital.

Police said the suspects were armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols and fled in two vehicles after allegedly robbing patrons of their cellphones.

The motive remains unknown.

Police have opened 17 murder cases, 15 counts of attempted murder and two of malicious damage to property.

World.title: Ekurhuleni Murders | Gayton McKenzie for action following tenth body found
World.content:
BLOEMFONTEIN - The Patriotic Alliance is urging police to catch those responsible for the Ekurhuleni murders.

This after another woman's body was found this time in Mooifontein Cemetery in Thembisa on Saturday morning.

It brings to ten the total number of women's bodies found there since July.

Patriotic Alliance leader Gayton McKenzie was delivering the keynote address at the PA's election manifesto launch in Bloemfontein.

''Patriots, I cannot start my speech without asking all of you to rise and observe a minute silence for all the women who have been killed recently in South Africa. Please rise, patriots. Thank you.

"We are also praying for strength and wisdom for our police and detectives tasked with finding these killers,'' he said.

World.title: Ekurhuleni Murders | 'It's a shame on the men of SA' - Ramaphosa on discovery of tenth body
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The killing of women in Ekurhuleni is a shame on the men of South Africa.

That's how President Cyril Ramaphosa described it after, yet another body was found in Thembisa earlier.

The victim was naked when her body was discovered at Mooifontein Cemetery.

It brings to ten the number of women found dead within the City of Ekurhuleni, in the past two months.

Police said more details will follow after preliminary investigations.

Ramaphosa was speaking while on the ANC campaign trail in eThekwini.

"Well, I've sadly heard about 10th body of a woman found in Thembisa. This continues to make us very sad and in many ways. It's a shame on the men of South Africa that we continue to kill the women of our beautiful country.

"We are essentially defiling that standing of our country as men. We are going to be making sure that there are a number of interventions that we will embark upon that will shine even a bigger light on all these dastardly acts that are continuing of men playing football with the lives of our women."

World.title: ANC is on a campaign trail in eThekwini
World.content:
ETHEKWINI - ANC senior leaders are stepping up their campaign in eThekwini, hoping to win back voters ahead of the November elections.

The party has seen its support decline in the metro in recent years.

ANC NEC member and eThekwini Mayor Cyril Xaba said the party's focus is on regaining lost ground.

"The president is in the city, in KwaZulu-Natal, and the response is positive. And of course, ground lost is not something you can then say is permanent. It's because people, many people, did not turn out to the voting station. And now we're encouraging them that these elections are a do or die.

"Therefore, they might come out in their numbers and defend this democracy. It is about the defense of our democracy. We can't leave it to chance. You make a mistake now; you regret it for the rest of your life."

World.title: Basic service delivery is not enough - ActionSA
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - ActionSA has said simply delivering basic services should not be seen as an achievement.

The party is unveiling its 2026 local government manifesto in Johannesburg.

Mary Phadi is a Nkangala district municipality candidate.

She said their focus is on fixing the municipalities behind ongoing service delivery failures.

"Giving people a service delivery is not an exception; it's not an achievement. People deserve water. What makes us unique is that we are saying that let us fix the broken municipalities that have caused us to be here after many years of democracy in our country.

"Today we are going to emphasise, this is the second time by the way, exchanges is contesting the local government elections and we've already proven ourselves where we have a mayoral candidate but today it's about to re-emphasise our key points in our policies to say we cannot sit back and do nothing when our communities need us most."

World.title: 18-year-old charged for false rape accusation
World.content:
KURUMAN – An 18-year-old woman was arrested in Kuruman by the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID) after she made a false rape accusation.

The young woman claimed a police constable raped her at a guest house on 23 September.

IPID's Lizzy Suping said the 24-year-old Constable was arrested on 24 September 2026 and faced a charge of rape.

"Prior to the police officer’s court appearance today, on 25 September 2026, the 18-year-old woman informed the IPID investigator that she had filed a false statement, because the officer failed to pay her, the agreed R400 that was due to her following their consensual sex," Suping said in a statement.

A case of perjury was opened against the 18-year-old woman for deliberately lying under oath and abusing state resources.

The rape case against the 24-year-old Constable was withdrawn in court.

"The actions of the 18-year-old woman undermine the integrity of the justice system and divert critical investigative capacity away from genuine cases.

"As IPID we would like to sensitize our communities that false reporting will not be tolerated, and decisive action will be taken against individuals who attempt to misuse the justice system for personal gain," Suping added.

World.title: Ekurhuleni Murders | Tenth woman's body found
World.content:
Editor's Note: This article was updated with new information after publication

THEMBISA – Police have found a woman's body at Mooifontein Cemetery in Thembisa.

The discovery of the semi-naked woman brings to ten the number of bodies found in the Ekurhuleni Metro in the last two months.

"A woman’s body has been discovered in Tembisa South, in the Vusimusi section, this morning, 26 September 2026. At this stage, we can only confirm the discovery of the body. This is a developing story.
