World.title: Iraq reaches 100,000 LPG converted cars as Parliament urges factory model access
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Gas Filling and Services Company, an operating affiliate of the Iraqi Ministry of Oil, announced on Saturday, September 26, 2026, that the cumulative number of vehicles converted to run on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has reached approximately 100,000 across Iraq.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the company’s media director, Mahdi Al-Nouri, confirmed that retrofitted vehicle figures currently range between 98,000 and 100,000 cars, noting an escalating pace of adoption among motorists seeking economical alternatives to conventional liquid fuels.

Al-Nouri stated that installation and technical maintenance services are carried out across a nationwide network of 26 specialized workshops operating under the state-owned gas company.

The growing consumer uptake reflects heightened public interest in cleaner, subsidized autogas, prompting the Ministry of Oil to scale up workshop throughput and expand fueling station capacity to keep up with escalating demand.

Despite this milestone, converted vehicles represent a modest fraction—less than 1.5 percent—of Iraq’s national automobile fleet, which currently totals approximately 7 million registered cars. The autogas initiative has simultaneously sparked parliamentary scrutiny regarding regulatory bottlenecks.

Lawmaker Amer Abdul-Jabbar raised the issue on the floor of the Council of Representatives, criticizing the Ministry of Oil for restricting autogas dispensing exclusively to locally converted vehicles while denying fuel to imported cars equipped with factory-installed LPG systems.

Abdul-Jabbar called on the federal government to reform existing fuel distribution policies, authorize gas sales for all compatible vehicles, and incentivize the commercial importation of factory-built LPG cars to accelerate emissions reduction and alleviate domestic gasoline consumption.

World.title: Iraq launches first smart pneumatic waste collection system with Spanish backing
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s National Investment Commission (NIC), in coordination with the Ministry of Environment and the Spanish Embassy in Baghdad, officially launched the country’s first smart automated pneumatic waste collection system (URD) on Saturday, September 26, 2026, marking a pivotal milestone in the modernization of municipal sanitation and sustainable urban management.

The initiative introduces advanced underground vacuum collection networks designed to eliminate conventional curbside dumpsters and heavy collection vehicular traffic across newly planned smart cities and licensed residential investment developments.

Speaking at the launch conference attended by an Iraqi News Agency (INA) correspondent, NIC Deputy Chairman Salar Mohammed Amin affirmed that the adoption of the URD pneumatic network represents a comprehensive national initiative requiring deep cross-institutional synergy between public ministries, municipal directorates, and private developers.

He revealed that the commission has already secured all statutory and regulatory approvals to mandate the underground system within master plans for new satellite cities and residential complexes, establishing a national technical committee alongside the Ministry of Environment to oversee phased execution and enforce strict environmental compliance benchmarks.

Amin emphasized that sustainable investment must transcend structural brick-and-mortar construction to create integrated, livable urban ecosystems that elevate daily public health and quality of life.

He noted that operational success relies on an interconnected institutional network encompassing the Ministry of Construction, Housing, Municipalities and Public Works, the Municipality of Baghdad, local governorate authorities, the Ministry of Electricity, and telecommunications operators, working collectively to provide dedicated power grids, subterranean civil infrastructure, and smart sensor integration necessary for automated municipal services.

Spanish Ambassador to Iraq Alicia Rico Pérez del Pulgar underscored that the rollout of the pneumatic vacuum infrastructure represents a substantial qualitative leap toward modernizing waste management practices through cleaner, more energy-efficient technologies.

Highlighting Madrid’s dedication to technical knowledge transfer and bilateral capacity building, the ambassador framed the project as a catalyst for expanded Spanish-Iraqi commercial and environmental partnerships in green infrastructure, renewable energy, and smart city urban planning, calling upon public institutions and private enterprises from both nations to leverage the project into enduring bilateral economic cooperation.

World.title: Iraq secures new US dollar cash shipment following Al Zaidi’s New York talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi reached formal understandings with U.S. authorities to secure the regular delivery of physical U.S. dollar cash shipments to Iraq, following bilateral and multilateral engagements alongside U.S. President Donald Trump in New York.

Government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi confirmed the development on Saturday, September 26, 2026, in an official statement reported by the 964 Network, indicating that high-level diplomatic contacts helped unblock logistical pipelines governing foreign currency transfers to the Central Bank of Iraq.

Al-Aboudi stated that a new installment of physical dollar currency is slated to arrive in Baghdad within the coming days, replenishing sovereign foreign exchange reserves and reinforcing domestic market liquidity.

The government spokesman emphasized that the agreement directly reflects substantial structural progress achieved by Iraqi monetary and fiscal authorities in tightening regulatory control over foreign currency distribution channels, enhancing transparency through the electronic trading platform, and preventing the illicit diversion of commercial liquidity.

The impending cash arrival comes at a critical juncture for Iraq’s parallel currency markets, where the dinar has steadily recovered toward the 157,000 range per $100 after trading near 160,000 earlier in September.

Iraqi financial officials anticipate that the scheduled cash injections, combined with comprehensive regulatory compliance recognized during the New York meetings, will help bridge the spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory peg of 131,000 dinars per $100 and stabilize domestic commodity pricing across the country.

World.title: AI startup urges optimism from Europe despite safety fears
World.content:
Freiburg im Breisgau – Europe needs to view artificial intelligence with more optimism — despite growing warnings about its dangers — or risk falling further behind, the head of a leading European AI start-up warned.

“I think the mindset in Europe needs to shift to one of optimism and to one of opportunity, and not to one of risk and fear,” Robin Rombach, CEO of German AI image generation specialist Black Forest Labs, told AFP.

Europe lags behind the United States and China when it comes to cutting-edge AI models. Policymakers and firms have been scrambling to find ways to make up lost ground.

But the debate has shifted to safety in recent weeks, after security lapses sparked calls from some industry leaders for development of the technology to be slowed down.

Based in the medieval German city of Freiburg, Rombach’s company — which takes its name from the nearby Black Forest — has emerged as a prominent developer of AI image-generation models.

The startup, valued at around $3.25 billion, recently hit the headlines when it announced US director Martin Scorsese as an advisor, prompting an angry response from some in Hollywood concerned about AI taking production jobs.

Rombach, 33, helped develop latent diffusion, a breakthrough that underpins many of today’s AI image-generation systems.

This propelled Rombach and a group of fellow computer scientists to found the AI lab in 2024. With just over 100 staff, its FLUX models generate still and moving images from text, and the company is now also expanding into physical AI.

Its latest model has been tested at carmaker Audi as part of a project aimed at enabling robots to perform production-line tasks.

Despite its roots in Freiburg — Rombach comes from the area — the firm’s ties to the United States and its tech scene are also strong.

The company has a second headquarters in San Francisco and secured early backing from Silicon Valley venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.

– ‘Stupidity’ is biggest risk –

Rombach said that when Black Forest Labs was founded, there was no “real startup ecosystem” in Europe, particularly for “frontier deep tech”.

“If you want to build a frontier model in a very competitive space, you need to do this quickly.”

“Certain ingredients” are needed for success, such as a lot of capital and computing power, he added.

As well as Black Forest Labs, Europe has other competitive AI companies, including France’s Mistral, but is still seen as trailing US firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic and Chinese labs such as DeepSeek.

Zach Meyers of CERRE, a Brussels-based think tank, echoed some of Rombach’s concerns, saying the “biggest barrier” to AI growth and innovation in Europe was access to capital.

Most European companies rely on financing from banks, which are traditionally more cautious than venture capital investors about backing businesses that may take years to become profitable, said Meyers, an expert in EU digital policy.

“That is not how technology markets work, particularly with a really nascent technology like AI,” he told AFP.

Safety concerns related to AI have escalated after incidents of the technology getting around controls during tests, sparking dire warnings from some about the threats that it poses.

Rombach emphasised his company’s focus on “open-weight” AI models, some of which can be downloaded by researchers and developers, “increases transparency, increases safety”.

He called for an open approach to AI development, warning it would be “fundamentally wrong” for such a crucial technology to be controlled by a few companies, rendering oversight more difficult.

But for Rombach, the biggest danger rests in potential human failings.

“The main thing that can wipe out humanity is stupidity,” he said.

World.title: Japanese anime actor fights TikTok over AI voice cloning
World.content:
Tokyo – A high-profile Japanese anime voice actor has taken TikTok to court over videos he says feature an artificial intelligence clone of his “lustrous” baritone, with a verdict due on Wednesday.

AI imitation is a growing concern among performers worldwide, and the threat has roiled Japan’s storied animation industry, whose voice actors are sometimes worshipped as much as their characters by fans.

The lawsuit filed by Kenjiro Tsuda, known for his starring roles in mega-franchises including “Jujutsu Kaisen” and “Yu-Gi-Oh!”, is believed to be the country’s first seeking to defend an individual’s vocal identity against AI-generated copies.

Tsuda is demanding TikTok remove a slew of videos narrated by a distinctively “deep” and “lustrous” voice that the 55-year-old says can only be his.

The platform however argues it is a “generic male voice” whose perceived similarity to Tsuda’s is subjective at best, according to court records accessed by AFP.

An actor’s voice “is the result of years of rigorous training and apprenticeship” to hone talent, Yuko Sasaki, executive director of the Japan Actors Union, told AFP.

“It’s something we spend lots of time and money perfecting,” said Sasaki, a fellow voice actor, adding that “we support Tsuda wholeheartedly”.

The court should “acknowledge that ownership of a voice is a fundamental right”, she said.

An anonymous account, whose picture resembled a “Jujutsu Kaisen” character dubbed by Tsuda, posted the videos in question.

They combined images and seemingly AI-generated speech about urban legends, occult phenomena and conspiracy theories.

The account at one point boasted more than 200,000 subscribers and would have brought in upwards of 500,000 yen ($3,200) in monthly revenue, the legal complaint argued.

– ‘Sordid content’ –

The account, whose posts mostly lacked original substance, “only gained popularity because its dubious, sordid content was narrated by the attractive voice of a popular actor,” Tsuda’s legal team said, according to the court records.

This infringes Tsuda’s so-called publicity rights — the ability to control and profit from the use of aspects of one’s identity — his attorneys said.

Although the account itself is no longer viewable on the platform, the Tokyo District Court will rule on whether TikTok was responsible for deleting the posts.

Parallel to the lawsuit, Sasaki and other Japanese voice actors have launched a campaign, called “No More”, against using generative AI to mimic performers without permission.

“Our industry can be crushed” if a court win for TikTok triggers “unbridled” AI voice cloning on social media, actor Bin Shimada told AFP.

That could cause younger actors to “lose hope”, said Shimada, who is part of the campaign group.

It is also fast becoming a global issue.

“In many countries copyright and data protection laws are not being adequately adapted” to protect performers from AI clones, the International Federation of Actors said last year.

ChatGPT maker OpenAI was forced to apologise in 2024 to star Scarlett Johansson over a synthetic voice that sounded like her, released after she declined to work with OpenAI on the project.

– International interest –

While no law explicitly enshrines a person’s voice in Japan, the justice ministry published legally non-binding guidelines last month clarifying its protection under existing rights.

As “the symbol of one’s personality” voice is subject to “publicity rights” and “rights to prevent unauthorised use of one’s portrait and likeness”, the ministry said.

But it remains to be seen whether and how the guidelines will influence Wednesday’s court decision on Tsuda’s case.

TikTok has questioned the actor’s “national fame”, rejecting his accusations that the account was free-riding on a well-known brand in a violation of Japan’s unfair competition prevention laws.

As a platform, all it did was “host a forum where users could post creative and ingenious content within the scope of free speech,” it told the court.

It is “very unlikely” that Tsuda’s voice will be outright denied publicity rights, Tatsuhiro Ueno, a professor of intellectual property studies at Waseda University, told AFP.

Given the actor’s “Jujutsu Kaisen” role as a stoic, elite sorcerer that made his voice “highly recognisable in Europe”, Ueno believes the verdict “will garner a lot of international interest”.

Veteran voice actor Michihiro Ikemizu, 83, also expressed solidarity with Tsuda — but said that AI, however sophisticated it gets, will never outperform human actors.

“You need to constantly feel and adapt while performing your role. That’s something AI can never do,” Ikemizu told AFP.

“That’s our only weapon.”

World.title: Spain beat England in Nations League to extend unbeaten run
World.content:
London – World champions Spain came from behind to beat England 3-2 in an entertaining Nations League encounter at Wembley on Saturday, denying the hosts a cathartic win after their painful World Cup exit.

Victory for Luis de la Fuente’s men extends Spain’s astonishing unbeaten run to 39 matches — a record for a European team.

England got off to a nightmare start when Lamine Yamal pounced on a gaffe by defender Marc Guehi, and they could easily have been three goals down as silky Spain created multiple chances.

But England, criticised for their ultra-defensive tactics in their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina, showed adventure of their own and got their reward in the 36th minute when Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon finished a fine team move.

Four minutes later Thomas Tuchel’s men were ahead after captain Harry Kane headed home Nico O’Reilly’s cross via a Marc Cucurella deflection.

Kane had a golden chance to give England a two-goal cushion from the penalty spot 10 minutes into the second half but slipped slightly, crashing his shot against the bar.

Spain, who beat England in the Euro 2024 final, took full advantage, with substitutes Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal both scoring to turn the match around.

De la Fuente said he felt his team had largely been in control against “superpower” England and he was confident they would have come back even from 3-1 down.

Asked about his side’s long unbeaten run, he said: “These are sensational moments…. Numbers are one thing, objective indicators are what we see. But what is important is that we still want to grow, we still want to improve.”

Kane bemoaned England’s inability to sustain their best level for the whole game.

“I spoke before that we reached good levels at the World Cup but didn’t quite put a full 90 minutes together,” he told ITV. “Probably similar again today.”

– Shaky start –

England boss Thomas Tuchel was adamant ahead of the match that it did not signal a new start but will have been dismayed at his team’s nervy start.

Manchester City’s Guehi, with a chance to clear in the second minute, inexplicably turned back towards goalkeeper James Trafford, apparently unaware that Yamal was just behind him.

The teenager pinched the ball and curled a left-footed effort off the inside of the post.

Ferran Torres was in the thick of the action, with an effort ruled out for offside and another shot saved by Trafford, in for long-time number one Jordan Pickford.

He also squandered a golden opportunity with just the goalkeeper to beat.

Yamal then set up Dani Olmo, who flashed wide as Spain rued yet another miss.

England, who had showed plenty of promise down the wings, made the visitors pay with an incisive counter-attacking goal after winning the ball back deep in their own half.

Gordon was involved early in the move and surged forward, collecting Jude Bellingham’s pass to steer the ball decisively past goalkeeper Unai Simon.

And, with the atmosphere now totally changed, England were in front when Kane rose to head home.

Tuchel’s men started the second half brightly and had a chance to extend their lead from the spot when they were awarded a penalty for a Rodri foul on Bellingham following a VAR check.

But Kane hit the bar and England paid the price when Baena steered home on the hour mark after O’Reilly had given the ball away to Olmo.

Worse was to come for the home side when Baena turned provider for Oyarzabal, who dinked the ball over Trafford.

Spain host Croatia in their next Nations League Group A3 match on Tuesday while England travel to the Czech Republic.

World.title: Oman calls for self-restraint, dialog in Mideast conflict
World.content:
United Nations – Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi called at the UN Saturday for “self-restraint” from all sides in the Middle East war, while stressing that Muscat was ready to mediate.

Earlier on Saturday, President Donald Trump rejected a truce deal proposed by Iran that Tehran said could have reopened the Strait of Hormuz to shipping within a week.

The waterway is key to the world’s energy supply and is now central to the conflict between the US and Iran, which is at a stalemate after nearly seven months.

“We call upon all parties concerned to settle their outstanding disputes through pursuing a policy of self-restraint and foresight, and through engaging in dialog to reach consensual, political solutions and sustainable understandings for the benefit of all,” Albusaidi said, addressing world leaders gathered in New York.

“Oman once again reaffirms its steadfast commitment to continuing its efforts aimed at safeguarding navigation in the Strait of Hormuz… We also call upon all parties to cooperate with Oman in these efforts.”

Oman sits across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, and ships seeking to skirt Tehran’s restrictions have recently been taking a route that hugs the Omani coast.

World.title: Mbappe out for two weeks or more with knee injury say Real
World.content:
Paris – France captain Kylian Mbappe suffered a hyperextension of his left knee playing for France, his club Real Madrid said Saturday but could be ready to play again when La Liga resumes.

“Following tests carried out today by Real Madrid’s medical department on our player Kylian Mbappe, he has been diagnosed with a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee,” the Spanish club said in a statement.

The forward left the pitch shortly after opening the scoring in a 1-0 French win against Turkey on Friday.

New France coach Zinedine Zidane said France were “not going to take any risks” and that he would not use Mbappe in the three Nations League matches scheduled over the next 10 days.

France travel to Belgium on Monday before hosting Italy and Belgium at the Stade de France on October 2 and 5.

Real Madrid’s first game after the international break, with Villarreal on October 10, might be too soon for an Mbappe return but Spanish daily AS reported Saturday he would ceratinly be ready for the Classico with Barcelona October 25.

World.title: Bengal SIR row: CM Suvendu Adhikari pins blame on Mamata for deletion of 27 lakh voters
World.content:
West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari has blamed former CM

for the deletion of around 27 lakh names from the stateâs electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), rejecting allegations that the BJP or the

was responsible.

Adhikari claimed the deletions were ordered by judicial officers following directions from the Supreme Court in a case filed by Banerjee herself. He accused the TMC leader of trying to shift responsibility after her defeat in the Assembly elections.

âThe responsibility for the deletion of 27 lakh names lies with Mamata Banerjee, not the BJP or the Election Commission. Judicial officers took the decision following the Supreme Court's directions in a case filed by her,â Adhikari said at a press conference.

The Election Commission has said 22.21 lakh of the deleted voters had filed appeals seeking their names to be restored. More than 38 lakh appeals have been filed in total against both exclusions and inclusions during the SIR process.

Politics over voter rolls

The SIR exercise has become a major political flashpoint in Bengal. The TMC has alleged that genuine voters were removed from the rolls and has demanded that their names be restored.

Adhikari, meanwhile, sought to contrast Bengal with Kerala, where the revision exercise has also taken place.





âIf SIR is good in Kerala, why is it bad in West Bengal? We have won 208 seats, while the two sides (TMC and its allies) have 80. Mamata Banerjee is unable to accept the people's verdict,â he said.

His comments came a day after Banerjee addressed a rally in Serampore and renewed her criticism of the Election Commission and the BJP over the voter-roll revision.

World.title: India, Canada seek to take ties ‘to a higher level’: EAM Jaishankar after UNGA meet
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India and Canada are looking to take their bilateral relationship to a âhigher levelâ, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said after meeting Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

âAlways a pleasure to meet FM @AnitaAnandMP of Canada #UNGA81 A productive discussion as we prepare to take the relationship to a higher level,â Jaishankar said in a post on X on Saturday.

The meeting comes as New Delhi and Ottawa work to rebuild ties and advance negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. The two sides have set a target of concluding the trade negotiations by the end of 2026.

Modi visit and trade deal in focus

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier this week that he expected Prime Minister Narendra Modi to visit Canada in December.

He also said negotiations on the trade agreement were making âgood progressâ.

âWe are making good progress in our trade negotiations with India. It is an exceptionally important relationship on many many levels, people-to-people levels, security levels, and also trade and economic,â Carney said at a press conference on the sidelines of the UNGA.

Carney was responding to questions about Modi's possible visit and the timeline for the trade agreement.





Canada had formally invited Modi to visit in 2026, with both governments agreeing to work through diplomatic channels to settle a mutually convenient date.

The possible December visit could coincide with the G20 Summit in Miami, which US President Donald Trump is scheduled to host on December 14 and 15.

India and Canada have been working to broaden cooperation beyond trade, including in energy, critical minerals, technology, defence and talent.

The two countries have also agreed to work towards a stronger strategic partnership.

Jaishankar holds more bilateral meetings

Jaishankar also met Venezuelan Foreign Minister Felix Plasencia Gonzalez during the UNGA. After the meeting, he said, âOur energy ties are gaining momentum, besides other areas of bilateral cooperation. We also discussed current regional issues.â

The meeting comes as India looks to diversify its energy supplies and strengthen relationships with oil-producing countries.

Jaishankar also held talks with Belarusian Foreign Minister Maxim Ryzhenkov and Mexican Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Alvarez on the sidelines of the UNGA.

World.title: ‘Old footage’: Delhi Police fact-checks viral Jantar Mantar protest video amid SIR row
World.content:
Debunked viral footage being circulated on social media

Protests over SIR row

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has debunked viral visuals of a massive protest being shared on social media, citing that it contains old footage from Jantar Mantar. They have also warned that legal action could be taken against those deliberately spreading misleading content.A video is currently being circulated on social media as showing a live, massive protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar. The video was shared by several accounts on X, including Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut, who claimed that protests against Kumar had begun in Delhi.Raut had shared the video with a caption saying, âProtests against Gyanesh Kumar Hatao have begun in Delhi, today's Jantar Mantar scene... A fight to the finish!âThe DCP New Delhi account on Saturday called the claim âfalseâ and said the footage was âarchived material from a past eventâ.âThe claim of a live, massive protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar today is false. The Video is Old: The footage being shared is archived material from a past event,â the Delhi Police said in a post on X.The police also warned that legal action would be taken against those found deliberately spreading misinformation or circulating misleading content.The video surfaced amid a widening political row over the Election Commissionâs Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Kumarâs resignation.The controversy intensified after a report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on decisions and procedures linked to the SIR exercise.Opposition parties have questioned the conduct of the revision and alleged irregularities, while the Election Commission has rejected the allegations.The Election Commission said on Saturday that decisions taken on SIR, including the nationwide exercise, were approved unanimously by the three-member poll panel. It also clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary concerned the functioning of an officer on deputation and was not related to any policy decision of the Commission.The poll panel also announced measures to ease the process for voters who receive notices over discrepancies, including allowing booth-level officers to visit their homes to collect documents and providing online hearings in exceptional cases. It said voters left out of the rolls, as well as young and first-time voters, can seek inclusion through the continuous updation process.The clarification over the viral video comes as opposition-led protests against the Election Commission have continued.The Indian Youth Congress marched from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar on Friday as part of a nationwide programme demanding Kumarâs resignation. Meanwhile, Peoples Democratic Party chief Mehbooba Mufti has called for a protest at Jantar Mantar on September 29, asking people to join a demonstration centred on democratic and secular values.The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has also threatened nationwide protests from October 2 if Kumar does not resign. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the agitation would begin in Mumbai on Gandhi Jayanti and then move to other cities.Opposition parties are also expected to discuss the SIR exercise and the functioning of the Election Commission at an INDIA bloc meeting on September 30.

World.title: SIR row: Congress' Khera questions EC over Form 6, says Bengal & Bihar polls ‘illegal’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Sunday questioned the

's response to concerns over Form 6, claiming that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was based on a change to the form that could not have been made without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

Speaking to news agency PTI, Khera said the rules could not be changed without being amended in Parliament and questioned whether the Election Commission had addressed the objections raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

"The 1960 Rules cannot be changed without being amended in Parliament. The biggest point of difference between Sandhu ji and Joshi with Gyanesh Kumar was this, and did we receive the answer to it today?" Khera said.

Questions Form 6 changes

Khera alleged that the SIR exercise was based on an "illegally changed" Form 6 and questioned the validity of elections conducted in Bengal and Bihar on the basis of the exercise.

"The entire SIR is based on a Form 6 that was changed illegally. The SIR that arose from that illegal form has also become illegal. The elections held in Bengal and Bihar based on that illegal SIR have also become illegal. Did we get an answer on this?" he said.





What is the Form 6 row?

The controversy centres on the requirement for new voters to provide details linking themselves or their parents or grandparents to electoral rolls from the previous SIR.

According to Indian Express reports, Election Commissioners Joshi and Sandhu had objected to incorporating the requirement into Form 6, arguing that the statutory form could not be altered without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

World.title: India seeks fair access to vaccines, drugs made from shared pathogens
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has called for a global system that ensures countries sharing pathogens and biological resources during a health emergency also get timely access to vaccines, diagnostics, medicines and technologies developed from them.

The demand was made at the UN High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response in New York, where India stressed that the credibility of the WHO Pandemic Agreement would depend on a fair Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing (PABS) system.

Union health secretary Punya Salila Srivastava said countries contributing pathogens should receive the benefits arising from their use, while respecting national sovereignty.

She also said ongoing negotiations on the PABS system should not be prejudged and that implementation should take into account national circumstances and capacities.

Drawing on its experience during Covid-19, India also called for digital public infrastructure to be recognised as a global public good, citing its role in disease surveillance, vaccination, risk communication, supply chains and continuity of health services during the pandemic.





India highlighted its contribution during Covid, saying it supplied 300 million vaccine doses to around 100 countries and two UN entities, besides providing medical assistance to more than 150 countries.

At the meeting, India also outlined measures to strengthen pandemic preparedness, including expanding laboratory networks, emergency coordination, the health workforce, stockpiles and clinical care capacity.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The WHO Pandemic Agreement, adopted in May 2025, is aimed at strengthening global preparedness for future pandemics. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for urgent completion of negotiations on the PABS system, saying delays could affect the world's ability to respond to future pandemics.

India stressed that pandemic preparedness must remain rooted in national health systems and domestic financing, with international assistance complementing national efforts. It also called for equity and global solidarity to remain central to preparations for future outbreaks.

World.title: ‘All SIR rollout decisions unanimous’: EC says agendas for all meetings to be circulated in advance
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

asserted Saturday that the decisions regarding special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken unanimously by chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

The statement came following the first meeting of the "full" Commission after a report in The Indian Express suggested the CEC disregarded the views of the two ECs on SIR-related calls, which sparked a political row, with the opposition targeting the govt and the CEC.

"The order for SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission," the EC said.

It also denied the claim that Sandhu and Joshi wrote to the Cabinet secretary to flag concerns over policy matters or IT processes.

SIR has been implemented in 20 states and UTs and is under way in 12 others. The poll panel also refuted the claim that Sandhu and Joshi wrote separate letters to the cabinet secretary to flag their concerns about policy matters or processes adopted by EC's IT division over which they no longer had control.





The letter was "related to the work of an officer on deputation to EC. The work re-distribution orders issued by the officer concerned were not actually implemented after the orders of the two commissioners and the oversight over the IT division by the DEC was never actually withdrawn," EC said.

The report said Sandhu and Joshi had called the move "a clear violation" of the law that governs EC and sought action against senior DEC Maneesh Garg, and linked the commissioners' objections to field officers allegedly being locked out of ECINET making it a "centralised" software directly controlled by EC.

The allegations linking the commissioners' objections to SIR and alleged lack of access to field officers to ECINET were seized upon by opposition to point their guns at the CEC. LoP Rahul Gandhi demanded he be imprisoned while opposition appeared set to seek his removal afresh.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Saturday's full commission meeting and the statement issued later sought to fix this; it cleared the air point by point, besides conveying the message that the three members had resolved their internal issues.

EC decided to concede on a slew of matters raised by the commissioners through internal notes, deciding that the agenda for all meetings shall henceforth be circulated in advance and the minutes issued. Also, annual performance appraisal reports of all officers would be completed by Dec 31 every year. The statement said all directions issued by the commissioners to the officers of the commission will be complied with and foreign trips for officers approved by the full commission.

On opposition's claim of disenfranchisement of 13 crore voters in SIR, EC said the final figure of electors will be known only after final publication of the roll in the remaining 12 states of Phase 3.

World.title: 2 more Naga men killed as ethnic violence flares up in Manipur again
World.content:
Two Mao Naga men were shot dead by unidentified gunmen at Kalenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district Saturday afternoon, with two others wounded, in the latest escalation in a Naga-Kuki conflict that has claimed more than 40 lives since Feb.

The shooting took place under Senapati police station around 2.30pm, shortly after CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh left a function about 30km away. It came two days after four Tangkhul Naga men were killed allegedly by Myanmar-based Kuki National Army-Burma (B) at Pilong village near the international border in Kamjong district.

The Kalenjang and Pilong killings are part of a series of Naga-Kuki clashes that began in Feb, shortly after Singh's govt took charge.

At least 21 people - 11 Nagas and 10 Kukis, including a pregnant woman - have been killed since Aug 27. The toll is separate from the Meitei-Kuki conflict, which has killed over 300.

Both the communities have accused militant groups from the other side of the attacks. Police have said several such allegations are under investigation and have not been independently verified.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The killings came as United Naga Council (UNC), the apex body of Naga tribes in Manipur, called off its 131-day economic blockade of NH-2 and NH-37 after a meeting with home ministry and Manipur govt at the BSF Frontier headquarters in Guwahati Saturday.





The blockade followed the abduction of six Liangmai Naga civilians in Kangpokpi district.

Manipur Congress president Okram Ibobi Singh accused BJP-headed NDA govts in the state and Centre of remaining "silent spectators" to civilian killings. "Govt is behaving as if it is not concerned about the killings of civilians of any community," the former three-time CM said. "We strongly condemn the killings of innocent civilians from Naga, Kuki and Meitei communities," he said, while questioning security along the Myanmar border.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE: Abhay Singh clinches squash silver after hard-fought final
World.content:
India endured a disappointing day in badminton at the Asian Games, with teenage sensation Unnati Hooda bowing out after a 16-21, 21-14, 17-21 quarterfinal loss to Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi, while women’s doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand also exited after losing 18-21, 9-21 to Malaysia’s Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan. Mixed doubles pair Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto completed the Indian exits, going down 14-21, 21-18, 18-21 to China’s world No. 1 Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dongping.

Abhay Singh secured a hard-fought silver medal in the men’s singles squash final at the Asian Games on Sunday (September 27, 2026), finishing runner-up to Malaysia’s Ng Eain Yow after a 3-0 defeat, with the final game ending 5-11. 18-year-old Anahat Singh staged a stunning comeback to defeat Japan’s Satomi Watanabe 3-2 in the semifinal and book her place in the women’s singles final, which is set to be played shortly. The singles winners will also earn direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

India will have a packed medal day on September 27 in Nagoya with shooters Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh and Rahi Sarnobat in action in women’s 25m pistol, long-jumpers Shaili Singh and Ancy Sojan in the women’s final.

Also read | Indian kabaddi teams dominate with double gold

Steeplechaser Parul Chaudhary and decathlete Tejaswin Shankar chasing podium finishes, while all eyes will be on badminton star P.V. Sindhu in the women’s singles quarterfinals and squash finalists Abhay Singh and Anahat Singh, who face Malaysian opponents for gold.

Also read | Anahat toughs it out against Satomi while Abhay breezes past Irfan

India enjoyed a productive day at the Asian Games on Saturday (September 26, 2026), adding multiple medals across kabaddi, athletics, shooting and squash, while securing berths in two squash singles finals. India have so far won 30 medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026, comprising four gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze medals.

World.title: Palle Panduga 3.0 set to be launched to transform rural roads
World.content:
Palle Panduga 3.0, the third edition in the series of rural development-oriented programmes conceived by the Andhra Pradesh State government, is all set to be launched in Andhra Pradesh by the Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and the Deputy Chief Minister Konidela Pawan Kalyan on Tuesday (September 29, 2026).

It is perhaps not without reason that the government has chosen the arid Ramapuram village in Varikuntapadu Mandal of the perennially drought-prone Udayagiri constituency (SPSR Nellore district) for the event as it clearly presents the current state of affairs in the village ahead of showcasing its impact after its transformation.

Teams led by Udayagiri TDP legislator Kakarla Suresh are slogging it out at the venue to make the statewide launch a grand success.

Speaking to the media, the MLA said the programme would entail laying of rural roads to a running distance of 8,571 km and involving an outlay of ₹5,838 crore, besides strengthening the drainage systems and building village administrative infrastructure such as Panchayat office buildings etc.

The launch of ₹12,000 crore worth of works under VB-G RAM G, that is, Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), would mean a lot in taking the fruits of the rural employment programme to the reach of beneficiaries, besides creating rural assets, he explained.

Projects worth ₹2,525 crore involving 4000 km of cement concrete roads, 22500 livestock shelters (mini Gokulam), 15,000 water storage units, one lakh farm pits were completed in the first phase, while 53,382 works worth ₹6787 crore involving 13,326 Panchayats were taken up in the second phase.

The third phase 3.0 involves completion of the works in progress through Panchayat level grants, providing drinking water connections through Jal Jeevan Mission and the pending rural road projects, including gravel roads to the farms.

Meanwhile, the ruling NDA alliance leaders of SPSR Nellore district are taking all measures to leave a lasting impact by mobilizing a huge crowd of one lakh in the presence of Mr. Naidu and Mr. Pawan Kalyan.

Several rounds of meetings were conducted over the last week in the presence of ministers Anam Ramanarayana Reddy, Ponguru Narayana, BC Janardhan Reddy, Gottipati Ravi Kumar, Member of Parliament Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy, district Collector Himanshu Shukla, Superintendent of Police Ajitha Vejendla among others.

The arrangements at the venue included ground leveling, shelter sheds for the crowd, drinking water facility, creation of parking lots etc.

MLA Mr. Suresh has announced to mobilize crowd from across Udayagiri, Varikuntapadu, Kaligiri, Vinjamur, Seetharamapuram, Duttalur and Kondapuram mandals forming part of his constituency.

World.title: Suvendu claims Mamata responsible for deletion of 27 lakh names in Bengal SIR, not BJP or ECI
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (September 27, 2026) blamed former CM Mamata Banerjee for the deletion of 27 lakh names from the State's electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision, asserting that neither the BJP nor the Election Commission could be held responsible for the exclusions.

Mr. Adhikari said the deletions were carried out by judicial officers pursuant to directions of the Supreme Court in a case filed by Ms. Banerjee herself, and accused her of attempting to shift the blame after losing the Assembly elections.

“The responsibility for the deletion of 27 lakh names lies with Mamata Banerjee, not the BJP or the Election Commission. Judicial officers took the decision following the Supreme Court's directions in a case filed by her,” Mr. Adhikari said at a press conference here.

The Chief Minister's remarks came amid a renewed political confrontation over the SIR exercise, with Ms. Banerjee's party alleging that genuine voters had been removed from the electoral rolls and demanding their restoration.

Mr. Adhikari also sought to turn the political argument over the SIR into a wider question of electoral accountability, accusing Banerjee of refusing to accept the verdict of the electorate.

“If SIR is good in Kerala, why is it bad in West Bengal? We have won 208 seats, while the two sides (TMC and its allies) have 80. Mamata Banerjee is unable to accept the people's verdict,” he said.

The chief minister's jibe came a day after Ms. Banerjee addressed a rally at Serampore and launched a fresh attack on the Election Commission and the BJP over the voter-roll revision.

Mr. Adhikari also referred to Saturday's meeting of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and two Election Commissioners — Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi — claiming that the meeting and the poll panel's subsequent statement showed that decisions relating to the Bengal SIR had not been taken by the CEC alone.

His assertion comes against the backdrop of a controversy over the functioning of the three-member Election Commission after an Indian Express investigation reported that the two election commissioners had raised objections on several occasions to decisions linked to the SIR exercise.

The commission, however, has maintained that differences in internal deliberations are normal and that its final decisions were unanimous.

World.title: 2024 Lok Sabha polls: DMDK’s Vijaya Prabhakaran to withdraw election petition against Congress MP Manickam Tagore’s victory
World.content:
Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK) youth wing secretary V. Vijaya Prabhakaran, has decided to withdraw an election petition filed by him before the Madras High Court in 2024 challenging the victory of incumbent Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president B. Manickam Tagore from Virudhunagar Lok Sabha constituency in the parliamentary elections.

In an application filed before Justice N. Sathish Kumar, Mr. Prabhakaran said he does not want to take the election petition for trial since he had decided to bestow his attention to public life rather than continuing the litigation pending for last two years. He sought the leave of the court, under Sections 109 and 110 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, to withdraw the election petition.

The judge has directed the applicant to issue notice to all the parties to the election petition besides issuing a publication in the official government gazette expressing his desire to withdraw the election petition to find out if any other eligible person was interested in substituting himself/herself in the place of the election petitioner in order to continue the challenge made to the victory of Virudhunagar MP Mr. Tagore.

Virudhunagar Lok Sabha constituency had witnessed a keenly contested three-cornered fight between Mr. Tagore, Mr. Prabhakaran and actor R. Radikaa Sarathkumar who was fielded as a candidate of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Mr. Tagore had polled 3,85,256 votes and defeated his nearest rival Mr. Prabhakaran by a slim margin of 4,379 votes with the latter securing as many as 3,80,877 votes.

In his election petition, Mr. Prabhakaran had accused Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer V.P. Jeyaseelan, who was the Returning Officer of Virudhunagar paliamentary constituency, of having succumbed to the pressure exerted by the then DMK Ministers K.K.S.S.R. Ramachandran, Thangam Thennarasu and P. Moorthy for furthering the prospects of the election of their then alliance party candidate Mr. Tagore.

Mr. Prabhakaran had also raised other grounds such as improper acceptance of nomination paper by claiming the MP had not disclosed all details regarding his assets and criminal cases. He had further accused the MP of having won the election by indulging in electoral corrupt practices such as bribing the voters through distribution of a ‘guarantee card’ and so on.

Paying cash for votes, booth capturing, malpractices during the counting of votes, improper rejection of postal ballots polled in favour of the election petitioner and alleged excess expenditure by the MP were the other grounds on which his election had been challenged. Mr. Tagore had taken out an application in 2024 itself to reject the election petition and strike off the allegations levelled against him.

The MP argued the guarantee card contained an assurance given by the Congress in its election manifesto and therefore such an assurance could not be termed as a corrupt practice. He also contended all the charges levelled against him were vague and do not necessitate a trial. However, Justice Kumar had on March 4, 2025 refused to reject the election petition and decided to take it up for trial.

World.title: Separate mass shootings in South Africa townships leave at least 27 people dead
World.content:
Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, police said Sunday (September 27, 2026).

The South African Police Service said 17 people were killed Saturday (September 26, 2026) night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, southwest of Johannesburg. At least 15 others sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.

In a separate statement, police said 10 people were killed in a mass shooting at a store in Lwandle, near Cape Town, around 1 a.m. Sunday (September 27, 2026). Another 11 were wounded in that shooting. Police said they were searching for multiple suspects in that case also, though they didn’t give an exact number.

The two shootings come just days after a mass shooting by three gunmen at a house party near the east coast city of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.

No arrests had been made in the two latest mass shootings, police said.

South Africa has struggled with high rates of violent crime for years, but the series of mass shootings this week were shocking even to a country used to some of the highest violent crime rates in the world.

World.title: MDR on UPI: SC to hear plea challenging imposition on September 28
World.content:
The Supreme Court will on Monday (September 28, 2026) hear a plea challenging the Centre's decision to impose a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on specified UPI person-to-merchant transactions of over ₹2,000.

Ending nearly six years of fully free UPI payments, the government has introduced a 0.4% fee on transfers worth over ₹2,000 made to merchants through the UPI platform from October 15 while explicitly ring-fencing everyday person-to-person transactions and small payments from any charge.

The MDR will be capped at ₹300 for payments of ₹75,000 and above.

Essential and thin-margin sectors — railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, and agricultural inputs — will pay a flat MDR of ₹5 per transaction above ₹2,000.

Payments into mutual funds, securities, and through stockbrokers and dealers will attract 0.02% MDR, also capped at ₹300.

Person-to-person (P2P) transfers — which make up 37% of UPI's transaction volume and 70% of its transaction value — will continue to attract zero charges, irrespective of size.

According to the apex court's cause list of September 28, the plea would come up for hearing before a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana.

The public interest litigation (PIL) filed by advocate Anjan Datta has challenged the Centre's September 14 notification and the MDR framework announced on September 15, which is stated to come into effect from October 15.

The plea alleged that the levy has been introduced without adequate statutory safeguards, transparency or public consultation.

It challenges the constitutional validity of the amended Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, alleging that it gives unguided powers to the executive to decide which electronic payment modes would receive the no-charge protection.

"Declare that no MDR or analogous compulsory charge may be imposed or recovered merely on the strength of a press release or FAQs absent a duly authorised, authenticated and published statutory instrument," it said.

The petitioner has also questioned the distinction between UPI transactions and RuPay debit card payments, pointing out that the notification continues the no-charge protection for RuPay debit cards without a monetary ceiling.

The plea alleges that the framework is arbitrary and discriminatory, and may adversely affect merchants, particularly those with low margins, while also raising concerns over possible indirect consumer burden and digital exclusion.

It has sought the quashing or suspension of the framework insofar as it imposes an MDR on UPI transactions of above ₹2,000.

Alternatively, it has sought a reconsideration of the framework after transparent consultation, publication of empirical data and an impact assessment, besides safeguards for micro and small enterprises.

"Direct that any future MDR classification be based on relevant considerations including merchant turnover, statutory MSME status, actual margins, geography and ability to bear the cost, and avoid cliff-edge treatment unsupported by evidence," the plea said.

It has made the Centre and others, including the Reserve Bank of India, as party respondents in the matter.

World.title: Two men die allegedly due to suffocation from chemical leak inside public toilet in Mumbai
World.content:
Two men died after allegedly suffocating due to a suspected chemical leak inside a public toilet near Mrunaltai Gore Bridge in Goregaon East early on Sunday (September 27, 2026), according to preliminary information from civic authorities.

The deceased have been identified as Prabhakar Dhanivar, 24, and Bhavin Desai, 18. Both were taken to Trauma Care Hospital, where a doctor declared them ‘brought dead’ at 3:49 a.m., according to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC).

Local residents said the two men had suffocated after encountering a strong chemical smell inside the toilet. The exact nature and source of the suspected chemical leak are being investigated.

World.title: Surgical strikes presented bold example of India's counter-terrorism policy: PM Modi
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (September 27, 2026) said the 2016 surgical strikes were India's decisive response to the pain of terror attacks and presented a bold example of the country's counter-terrorism policy.

Asserting that India follows a policy of zero tolerance against terrorism, he said in his monthly broadcast 'Mann Ki Baat' that the country has made it clear that terrorism will be met with a strong and decisive response.

Mr. Modi said on September 28-29, 2016, the Indian Army conducted surgical strikes on terror hideouts across the Line of Control (LoC) following a terror attack on an Army camp at Uri in Jammu and Kashmir.

He said the way the brave soldiers of India crossed the LoC and took action against terrorism left the world stunned.

"India has made it clear that terrorism will be met with a strong and decisive response. The surgical strike presented a bold new example of India's counter-terrorism policy right in front of the entire world," he said.

The Prime Minister said India endured pain for a long time due to terrorist attacks and the surgical strikes were the country's decisive response against that agony.

"India is following the policy of zero tolerance against terrorism," he asserted.

The Indian Army carried out surgical strikes against terror launch pads across the LoC following the terror attack on an Army camp in Uri.

PM encourages active participation in Census

Referring to the ongoing Census exercise, Mr. Modi said Census is a national responsibility and every citizen has a role to play.

He also asked everyone to avail the online enumeration facility during the Census exercise.

Talking about the fight against narcotics, the Prime Minister said India's youth are coming together against drugs.

"Through the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan' [Drug-free initiative], the youth are spreading awareness through creative campaigns and activities," he said.

Mr. Modi said during the 'Drug-Free Youth Campaign', millions of youth across the country have taken a very important pledge against addiction and drugs.

"The youth have themselves pledged to stay away from drugs and have also taken the responsibility to spread this message to others," he said.

During the address, the Prime Minister also paid tribute to late VHP leader Ashok Singhal on his birth anniversary on Sunday, and said he lived a life like an ascetic while remaining in society.

"The direction he gave to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, the energy he infused into it -that very result is what we are witnessing today as we see the grand temple in Ayodhya come to life before our eyes," he added.

World.title: Iran stands firm on Hormuz plan after US rejection
World.content:
Iran stood firm Sunday on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, despite US President Donald Trump’s rejection of the proposal that had created some optimism for breaking the Mideast war stalemate.

The waterway is key to the world’s energy supply and is now central to the conflict between Washington and Tehran, which was triggered nearly seven months ago with deadly strikes on Iran.

Iran’s plan called for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, and fulfilling conditions in the ceasefire deal that fell apart months ago.

That agreement, which dissolved during fighting over Hormuz, called for the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade.

“Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent upon these conditions being fulfilled. We will not back down from them,” Araghchi said on Sunday, state broadcaster IRIB reported.

“We have never closed the door to diplomacy or negotiations, but at the same time, we have never backed down from our rights.”

But Trump said on Saturday that he rejected the truce deal.

“They want to make a deal where they open the Strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” he told reporters. “They want to make a deal and I think that’s fine. I like making a deal too.”

Araghchi said on Sunday that the Iranians “saw the first reaction from the US president, but so far, nothing has been conveyed to us by the mediators”.

“We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive positions to us, and we will make a decision based on them,” the foreign minister added.

‘Tool for pressure’

Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, to reopen the strait and to launch talks on Iran’s nuclear programme.

But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway.

Iran requires ships to obtain authorisation before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons.

Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.

At the UN, Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan complained that the “international community has been absent” and is failing to live up to the responsibility to keep the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab open.

“The kingdom rejects any party’s use of these vital passages as a tool for pressure, threat, or harm to the interests of states,” he said, stressing the waterways’ importance to global energy security.

His Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov, told member states that “Russia, together with other responsible states, stands ready to constructively contribute to stabilising this strategically important region.”

In New York, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, according to his office, and said: “Iran has not walked away from the negotiating table but, given past experiences, it no longer trusts the United States.”

Araghchi said at the UN: “Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days.”

“The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure,” he added.

Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, was quoted by Tasnim news agency as saying: “We will not cease punishing the US until Iran’s seven conditions are met.”

Mohebi had told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Tehran’s demands.

World.title: IHC voids law allowing agencies to curb travel
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has declared unconstitutional a provision of the Passport Rules, 2021, that allowed the placement of a citizen’s name on the Passport Control List (PCL) on the recommendation of government agencies or departments without identifying a competent authority or providing legal safeguards.

Justice Raja Inaam Ameen Minhas, in a detailed judgement, declared the second limb of Rule 22(2)(b) ultra vires the Passports Act, 1974, and Articles 4, 9, 10A and 15 of the Constitution, holding that it was of no legal effect.

The judgement was issued on a petition filed by Moinuddin, who was offloaded at Islamabad International Airport on Dec 18, 2025, while travelling to Saudi Arabia for Umrah. He possessed a valid Pakistani passport, a valid Saudi visa and a confirmed air ticket, but no reason was communicated to him for stopping him from travelling.

The court noted that his passport had never been impounded, confiscated, cancelled or inactivated, nor had its issuance or renewal been refused. The dispute, therefore, centred on the question whether the agency had the authority to restrain a citizen from travelling on a valid passport.

According to the judgement, his name was placed on the PCL on Dec 24, 2024, on the recommendation of NCB-INTERPOL, forwarded by the FIA’s Assistant Director (Immigration Wing). The action followed his deportation from the UK after his conviction for causing death by dangerous driving while under the influence of alcohol. He had served a three-year sentence.

The court noted that he had completed his sentence and been deported, while no criminal case, inquiry or investigation was pending against him in Pakistan. He was neither a proclaimed offender nor the subject of an extradition request.

The IHC rejected the justification provided by the passport authorities to retain his name on the PCL that his conduct had adversely affected Pakistan’s reputation and that the placement was intended to create deterrence.

The court observed that these grounds were not contained in the Passports Act or the Passport Rules. Rule 21 dealt with refusal of a passport and did not authorise restraint of a citizen who already possessed a valid passport, the judgement stated.

“The refusal of a passport and the prohibition of travel are two separate exercises of power,” Justice Minhas observed, declaring that the function of the relevant division and directorate general to “prepare and maintain” the PCL was administrative and did not itself confer jurisdiction to decide whose name could be placed on the list.

The court pointed out that Rule 22(2) referred to individuals whose passport facilities had been refused. Moinuddin had never been refused a passport. It also noted that Rule 22(2)(a) specifically identified the additional secretary of the relevant division as the authority competent to place and remove names in Category A, whereas clause (b) identified no such authority.

The IHC held that neither the directorate general of FIA nor NCB-INTERPOL possessed the authority to place the petitioner’s name on the PCL in the circumstances of the case.

It observed that the impugned order merely stated that it had been issued with the approval of the “competent authority” without identifying that authority, the legal provision invoked or the material on which the decision was based.

The court found that the impugned provision provided no competent authority, objective criteria, notice, hearing, reasons or communication of the decision, meaning that a citizen could learn of the restriction only after being stopped at the immigration counter.

The judgement declared the second limb of Rule 22(2)(b) — allowing PCL placement on the recommendations of government agencies or departments — beyond Sections 8 and 13 of the Passports Act and inconsistent with the Constitution.

About the reasons of “international reputation” and “deterrence”, the court held that since the petitioner had completed his sentence and no proceedings were pending against him, the restraint had no “live and proximate nexus with a present necessity”.

“Gravity does not supply jurisdiction,” it said.

Expressing displeasure over the authorities’ failure to comply with an earlier order, the IHC directed them to decide the petitioner’s application within one week through a speaking and well-reasoned order.

The court consequently set aside the Jan 26, 2026, order of the agency and declared the petitioner’s placement on the PCL on Dec 24, 2024, without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

It directed the authorities to remove his name from the PCL within 15 days of receiving a certified copy of the judgement and not to interfere with his lawful foreign travel on the basis of the impugned placement.

The court clarified that the competent authority could still take action warranted by law after following the prescribed procedure. Copies of the judgement were sent to the Interior Secretary, Immigration and Passports DG and FIA DG for compliance.

Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

World.title: Polling underway in NA-168 Bahawalpur by-election
World.content:
BAHAWALPUR: Polling was underway on Sunday in the NA-168 Bahawalpur by-poll, with a close contest expected between PML-N’s Malik Munir Iqbal Channar and independent candidate Wali Dad Cheema.

Polling began at 8am and is expected to conclude at 5pm. Spokesperson for the Election Commission of Pakistan, Huda Gohar, told Dawn that voters present within the boundaries of the polling station will be allowed to cast their vote past 5pm as well.

The constituency fell vacant after the death of Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar in August, whose son is now the ruling party’s candidate.

According to data from the provincial election commissioner’s office, a total of 483,143 people are registered in the constituency, including 248,259 men and 234,614 women across 292 polling stations. At the polling stations, 307 presiding officers and 941 polling officers and assistant presiding officers have been deployed.

A day earlier, the Punjab Home Department requested the federal interior ministry that troops of army and Rangers (Punjab) be deployed in the constituency for smooth, peaceful and secure conduct of the by-election.

Leading up to the by-poll, three persons were injured on Sept 12 in an armed clash at Baqirpur in connection with the election campaign of Cheema, the son of former PML-Q federal minister Tariq Bashir Cheema.

As per Rescue 1122 sources, the clash occurred during Cheema’s election rally between the supporters of the rival candidates, and some of them resorted to firing, resulting in injuries to three people.

World.title: Terrorists take 13 people hostage in Bannu
World.content:
BANNU: Terrorists allegedly took 13 people hostage on Friday as they were moving to a safer location due to the ongoing tensions between a local peace committee, police and militants in the mountainous Hathikhel area of Wazir subdivision, local sources said.

According to sources, the people were stopped while they were transporting their belongings in vehicles to leave the area.

The hostages were identified as four brothers, Rehmanullah, Farmanullah, Laiq and Sadiq; Mir Ali, Mohammad Raziq, Azim Khan and three brothers, including Sameen, Hamidullah and Rakhidullah. Three other individuals could not be identified.

Police have not issued an official statement regarding the incident. However, police sources confirmed the incident.

Meanwhile, a photograph purportedly showing the alleged hostages has also circulated on social media.

The photograph also appears to show Nasir alias Gidarh, a local commander of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. The photograph and the identities of those shown in it could not be independently verified.

Local sources said terrorists were allegedly trying to prevent residents from leaving the area and had imposed certain restrictions on those seeking to relocate.

According to the sources, some families who failed to comply with the conditions allegedly had their houses demolished. These claims, however, could not be officially confirmed.

The deteriorating security situation in Hathikhel and adjoining mountainous areas has continued to cause difficulties for residents, with several families reportedly moving to safer locations.

Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

World.title: Three booked for rape of Azeri woman in Lahore
World.content:
LAHORE: Defence-C police on Saturday registered a case against three unidentified men on charges of subjecting an Azeri woman to gang rape.

A 20-year-old Azeri woman was visiting Pakistan for business purposes and was residing in a house near Raiwind Road.

She filed an application with the police stating that two women approached her for dinner. They went to a café where three men met them. She could identify the men and women by face.

She said the men offered her and two other women to drive and they later took her to an unidentified flat. She said they consumed alcohol and she was also served some intoxicating material and fell unconscious.

She said three men allegedly gang-raped her and later locked her in the flat till 2pm.

She said the suspects came back and dropped her near Ghazi Interchange and fled the scene.

She said the suspects also took away her mobile phone and other luggage. She demanded action against the suspects.

Defence-C police registered a case against the three suspects and started the investigation.

Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

World.title: China sends 2 giant pandas to US after Washington summit
World.content:
China sent two giant pandas to the United States on Sunday, state media said, after a Washington summit that was heavy on symbolism and light on breakthroughs.

The pandas’ transfer had already been agreed, but the departure was announced on Thursday during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington.

The black and white mammals are immensely popular around the world, and China loans them out as part of a “panda diplomacy” programme to foster foreign ties.

Ping Ping and Fu Shuang departed from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport on a chartered flight at around 3:00 am on Sunday (12am PKT on Saturday), state news agency Xinhua reported.

Steamed corn buns, bamboo shoots and carrots have been prepared to keep the pandas nourished during their 15-hour flight, Chinese state-run media outlet the Global Times reported.

The Boeing 777 operated by FedEx was the top-tracked aircraft on aviation information platform FlightRadar24 as it neared Alaska, roughly halfway into its journey.

The pandas are headed to a zoo in Atlanta, Georgia, where they will be spending the next 10 years.

A farewell ceremony was held for the pair before their departure by the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding.

Experienced keepers were dispatched by the US side to accompany the duo on their flight, the Global Times reported.

In preparation for their arrival, Zoo Atlanta has renovated its panda facilities and assembled a team of animal caretakers.

It has also ensured a stable and long-term supply of bamboo, grown locally in Atlanta, which has a climate that is very similar to Chengdu.

Zoo Atlanta previously hosted pandas on loan from China for a quarter of a century starting in 1999, but it has not had any since 2024.

Both the expected arrivals were born in 2020. Ping Ping, a male, is now six years old, while Fu Shuang, a female, will turn six next month.

Pandas in captivity typically live for around 30 years.

The furry creatures have been sent across the globe for decades as soft-power ambassadors of Beijing’s diplomatic goodwill.

In 1972, China gifted a pair of pandas to Washington, following US President Richard Nixon’s historic visit.

Beijing recalled two of its pandas from Japan early this year, following a diplomatic spat that began when Japan’s prime minister hinted that Tokyo could intervene militarily in the event of any attack on Taiwan.

World.title: Karachi ATC acquits 7 more policemen ‘for lack of evidence’ in Naqeebullah Mehsud's murder case
World.content:
KARACHI: After the acquittal of former Malir SSP Rao Anwar, an antiterrorism court on Saturday acquitted seven more policemen in a case over the killing of Naqeebullah Mehsud and three others in a staged encounter in January 2018.

The then SHOs of Shah Latif Town and Sachal police, Amanullah Marwat and Shaikh Muhammad Shoaib alias Shooter; assistant sub-inspector (ASI) Gada Hussain; head constables Sadaqat Ali and Mohsin Abbasi; and constables Raja Shamim and Rana Riaz Ahmed were facing trial for allegedly killing Naseemullah, better known as Naqeebullah Mehsud, Mohammad Sabir, Nazar Jan and Mohammad Ishaq in an alleged staged encounter in January 2018.

After examining the witnesses and hearing concluding arguments from both sides, the judge of ATC-VI exonerated the accused persons for lack of evidence.

Prosecutor Anila Malik argued that the prosecution examined over 40 witnesses, including star witnesses and they linked the accused persons with the commission of offences and documentary evidence also corroborated their testimonies.

Former SSP Rao Anwar was acquitted in the same case in 2023

She also contended that the prosecution established its case against all the accused persons beyond a shadow of reasonable doubt and pleaded for conviction.

However, defence lawyer Farzana Mateen submitted that all accused persons facing trial were framed with mala fide intention and that out of 40, not a single witness directly implicated any of the accused in the case.

She also maintained that there were glaring contradictions in the evidence of prosecution witnesses while two star witnesses about the abduction of Hazrat Ali and Muhammad Qasim did not associate the present accused persons in their statements recorded under Section 164 CrPC by a judicial magistrate and had also not identified these accused persons as the culprits during their evidence before the trial court.

The defence lawyer further argued that there was no allegation of abduction of the deceased against the accused persons and the prosecution has also failed to prove their participation in the alleged encounter.

She maintained that many accused persons, including a former senior superintendent of police, had already been exonerated by the trial court in the first round of litigation for want of evidence and she pleaded for acquittal of the present accused persons as well.

Initially, the then SSP Malir Rao Anwar, along with his around two dozen subordinates, had been booked for allegedly murdering Naqeebullah and others in an alleged staged encounter in a Malir locality and dubbing them as militants.

According to the prosecution, Naqeebullah was picked up with his two friends allegedly by eight to nine subordinates of Rao Anwar in civvies. Later, the other two detainees were set free while the whereabouts of Mehsud remained unknown and his mobile phone was also found powered off, as the former SSP allegedly kept him in wrongful detention.

It further stated that on Jan 17, the captive’s relatives came to know through the media that Rao Anwar and his associates allegedly killed Mehsud and three others in a staged encounter in a Shah Latif Town area on Jan 13 and dubbed them as Taliban militants.

The provincial police officer had constituted a three-member inquiry committee that found Rao Anwar and his associates involved in the case, it added.

However, in January 2023, the trial court acquitted the former SSP and 17 members of his team by extending the benefit of doubt. As the state had opted not to impugn the acquittal order, a brother of Naqeeb had filed an appeal before the Sindh High Court against their acquittal.

The present accused persons were absconders during the first trial, and after the exoneration of SSP and others, they had surrendered before the court to face the trial, and all of them were set free on bail in April this year.

Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

World.title: Captain Safdar sparks fresh debate over authenticity of lawyers’ degrees
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Weeks ahead of the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) elections, spouse of the Punjab chief minister retired Captain Mohammad Safdar has sparked a fresh debate over the authenticity of lawyers’ degrees, particularly those of candidates contesting the association’s top office.

The SCBA elections are scheduled for Oct 29, with the Independent Group, also known as the Asma Jahangir Group, fielding Syed Amjad Ali Shah as its presidential candidate, while the Professional Group, led by Hamid Khan, has nominated Sardar Aman Khan for the slot.

Meanwhile, Mr Safdar has announced the formation of his own group, the Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah Group, and invited lawyers to join it.

He said his group also intended to contest the SCBA elections.

Talking to media persons, Mr Safdar alleged that the law degree of one of the candidates for the SCBA presidency was fake and demanded its verification.

He also called for verification of the degrees of prominent lawyers, including Ahsan Bhoon, a close associate of Federal Law and Justice Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar.

Mr Bhoon, a former SCBA president, is currently a member of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan and heads the Independent Group.

Mr Safdar further alleged that some prominent lawyers charged their clients on a “done basis”, a term used for arrangements in which lawyers allegedly demand hefty fees while assuring clients of a 100pc favourable court decision.

He said such practices needed to be stopped and lawyers with dubious credentials should be removed from the legal profession.
